detail.abstract:
Fiscal systems generate millions of discrete events—tax filings, cross-border disclosures, school-boundary checks, inheritance triggers—that appear fragmented in most empirical work. This paper proposes Fiscal Event Geometry, an X-axis / Y-axis coordinate framework that represents such events as points in a two-dimensional fiscal space: the X-axis encodes cross-jurisdictional position in pre-tax public capital, while the Y-axis encodes intergenerational carrying capacity of post-tax private capital. By mapping events to coordinates rather than categories, the framework treats institutional movement not as narrative sequences but as trajectories, discontinuities, and clusters situated in a common state space.

Within this geometry, individuals and households frequently shift from primarily cross-border positions (X-dominant) to intergenerational positions (Y-dominant), and these “jumps” themselves become observable expressions of institutional tension. The paper outlines a conceptual data-generating process in which fiscal rules trigger events, events update X-Y positions, and the resulting point cloud exhibits collective properties—densities, paths, and structural breaks—that can be studied econometrically.

Computational details, including weighting schemes, functional forms, and index construction (e.g., institutional-tension measures derived from this space), are implemented in proprietary CrossLab modules and are not disclosed here. The contribution is therefore architectural rather than algorithmic: establishing the coordinate system and event logic that make subsequent estimation, modeling, and index design possible.

By reframing tax administration and related infrastructures as generators of an event-level geometry rather than static background constraints, Fiscal Event Geometry provides a foundational state space for future work on institutional tension, cross-border governance, and intergenerational inequality.

title: Discrimination by Presumption: The Risk of Assuming Gender Bias when There is None
affiliations: University of Wyoming, University of Pennsylvania Perelman School of Medicine and George Mason University

detail.title: Discrimination by Presumption: The Risk of Assuming Gender Bias when There is None
detail.abstract: While it is evident that women as a group suffer when biases against them exist, we investigate consequences of gender biases being presumed but not actually present. In our experiment, employers hire experts who sell advice to customers. We find that employers believe that customers prefer advice from male experts over advice from equally qualified female experts. Therefore, employers favor hiring males. Customers, however, actually value advice from male and female experts about the same. When employers' beliefs are corrected, their bias toward hiring men disappears. Our results show risks of exaggerating, or presuming the existence of, gender bias.

title: Spiritual Capital: A Micro-Foundational Approach
affiliations: University of Rome Tor Vergata - Faculty of Economics

detail.title: Spiritual Capital: A Micro-Foundational Approach

declarations.ethicsApproval: The paper has no empirical work. Ethical approval does not apply

detail.abstract: This paper proposes a micro-foundational and dynamic definition of spiritual capital and situates it within the broader literature in economics, sociology, and psychology. We define spiritual capital as the accumulated stock of inner resources-discernment, relational intelligence, emotional intelligence, and contemplation-inaction that equip individuals to live with purpose and to contribute to the common good. We further sketch the idea of a stock-flow model in which spiritual capital is formed through bottom-up experiential learning and top-down nourishment from religious or philosophical traditions. This framework reconciles religious and secular understandings by showing that most lay (non-religious) and religious components of spiritual capital overlap. We link spiritual capital to civic freedom, relational goods, and generativity, and we connect the concept to prior empirical findings on religion and happiness, relational intelligence and well-being, and freedom and subjective well-being. In doing so, the paper provides a more operational and inclusive account of spiritual capital that can support future empirical measurement and policy-oriented research.

title: Procedural Rationality, Endogenous Sampling, and the Instability of Defection
affiliations: Indian Institute of Technology (IIT), Kanpur and Kyoto University - Institute of Economic Research

detail.title: Procedural Rationality, Endogenous Sampling, and the Instability of Defection
detail.abstract: We examine cooperation and defection in populations where individuals use both procedural rationality and imitation to choose their strategies. For a broad class of sampling-based choice procedures that encompass both procedural rationality and imitation, we characterize the conditions under which universal defection becomes unstable. The results highlight that for cooperation to emerge and persist, the manner in which agents generate and share information can be as important as the underlying payoff incentives.

title: Stoic Principles as an Integrative Approach to Stress Management for Executives: An Extended Theoretical Model

detail.title: Stoic Principles as an Integrative Approach to Stress Management for Executives: An Extended Theoretical Model

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest.
declarations.funderStatement: No external funding.

detail.abstract: Executives operate in increasingly complex, fast-paced, and digitally saturated environments that generate substantial and persistent stressors. These conditions impair cognitive clarity, emotional stability, and interpersonal functioning. While established stress-management programs demonstrate effectiveness in controlled contexts, many of these approaches are difficult to maintain in the dynamic routines of executive roles. Stoic philosophy provides a theoretically grounded and practically accessible framework that links cognitive appraisal, emotional differentiation, and value-based self-leadership. This article develops an extended theoretical model-drawing on psychological stress research, biological activation models, sociological perspectives on occupational strain, and core Stoic principles-to illustrate how Stoic practices can mitigate chronic stress among executives. The model clarifies how Stoic thinking promotes more adaptive cognitive evaluations, strengthens emotional regulation, and enables sustained value-driven action. Stoic principles thereby offer an accessible and integrative approach for fostering resilience and long-term psychological stability within executive leadership.

title: Operation Optimization for Storage Allocation and Request Scheduling in Multi-Deep Four-Way Shuttle Storage and Retrieval Systems

detail.title: Operation Optimization for Storage Allocation and Request Scheduling in Multi-Deep Four-Way Shuttle Storage and Retrieval Systems
detail.abstract: This paper studies the operation optimization problem of continuously arriving batched requests in the multi-deep four-way shuttle storage and retrieval system. In such a system, the dynamic state changes of racks and the assignment between requests and logistics equipment can generate different transportation routes and extra operation tasks during the operation process. The storage space allocation and request scheduling within each operation cycle are important issues to improve the system efficiency. Therefore, we propose an integrated optimization method that performs the operation tasks in batches. For each batch, the method first determines the optimal assignment of racks and load/unload points for all loads, considering the balance between the current operations and future requests, and then assigns lifts and shuttles to execute the assignment schemes with the objective of minimizing the makespan. A mathematical model is formulated and a multi-objective differential evolution algorithm with simulated annealing mechanism is designed to solve the assignment problem. The experimental analysis shows that the proposed method and algorithm consistently exhibit competitive performance. Compared to assignment methods used in practice and in the literature, our proposed method can reduce the makespan considerably. Furthermore, we analyze how demand skewness and batch size affect the makespan, showing evidence that the proposed method can help to optimize storage allocation and request scheduling in batches and achieve a small makespan during the operation process.

title: Exploring the Challenges of University Council Independence in Ghana’s Higher Education Architecture
affiliations: University of Education, Winneba, University of Education, Winneba, University of Cape Coast and University of Education, Winneba

detail.title: Exploring the Challenges of University Council Independence in Ghana’s Higher Education Architecture

publicationDetails.detailsText: African Quarterly Social Science Review, volume 2, issue 4, 2025[10.51867/AQSSR.2.4.40]

detail.abstract: This study explores the challenges of university council independence in Ghana's public universities, prompted by proposed legislative reforms increasing government oversight. The study is anchored on the principal-agent theory. Using an exploratory qualitative design, semi-structured interviews were conducted with 30 key informants, including government, faculty members, non-faculty members, and student representatives from Ghana's five oldest public universities. Thematic and document analysis revealed that government influence, through regulatory constraints, financial control, and appointment powers, restricts council autonomy. It is proposed that independent funding boards must be created to monitor the flow of funding, which will lessen dependency on government subsidies. Public-private partnership initiatives, which encourage industrial partnerships to finance infrastructure and research, should be promoted. To ensure fair representation and diminish political influence, public universities must set clear guidelines for council appointees. Additionally, efforts should be made to implement fee regulation mechanisms, such as limiting tuition hikes and expanding student scholarship opportunities, particularly under increased university autonomy. By highlighting the necessity of striking a balance between autonomy and accountability, these findings contribute to the global discourse on higher education governance.

title: On Certain Legal Features of Arbitration Organization in the Republic of Kazakhstan

detail.title: On Certain Legal Features of Arbitration Organization in the Republic of Kazakhstan

detail.abstract: The contemporary model of arbitration in the Republic of Kazakhstan (RK) represents a balanced system based on the legislatively enshrined autonomy of the parties and limited judicial control. The article analyzes the key parameters of this model, ensuring its practical effectiveness in commercial turnover. The issues of institutional transparency, qualification requirements for arbitrators, and procedural flexibility of proceedings, including multi-format hearings, are examined. Special attention is paid to the boundaries of arbitrability of disputes involving the public sector: the mechanism of preliminary consent of the authorized body is considered, as well as its non applicability in relations with non-residents, which is a key element of the policy to strengthen the investment attractiveness of the jurisdiction. It is demonstrated how the infrastructure of the Astana International Financial Centre (AIFC), including the AIFC Court, complements the arbitration system with flexible tools for judicial support and enforcement. The author concludes that the Kazakhstan arbitration configuration ensures a stable balance between the freedom to design the procedure and institutional predictability, which enhances the manageability of commercial risks.

title: Public Prayer as Symbol: Competing Social, Political, and Religious Interpretations in Italy (2000–2025)
affiliations: Centre for the Study of Minority Cultures & Law

detail.title: Public Prayer as Symbol: Competing Social, Political, and Religious Interpretations in Italy (2000–2025)

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None
declarations.funderStatement: None

detail.abstract: This book chapter examines the phenomenon of public Muslim prayer in Italy between 2000 and 2025, situating it within the broader processes of urban religiosity and public space management. While the topic has relevance for all newly developing multicultural countries (NDMCs) in the Western world, Italy serves as a case study for understanding how religious practices intersect with civic life, political authority, and social perceptions. Historically, Italian public spaces have been religified-made sacred or symbolically charged-through Christian rituals such as Easter processions, patron saint festivals, and other public rites. In recent decades, however, public space has increasingly hosted Islamic religious expression, including congregational street prayers, Eid celebrations in open areas, and spontaneous acts of worship such as bus drivers stopping on the road to pray. This study employs a multi-layered analytical framework, integrating scholarly literature, media accounts, and policy responses. It examines the symbolic meanings ascribed to public prayer by multiple stakeholders: municipal and national authorities, Catholic institutions, Muslim community leaders, and civil society. The research highlights competing interpretations-for some, public Muslim prayer is an expression of religious freedom and integration; for others, it signals political assertion, challenges secular norms, or provokes societal anxiety. The book chapter also explores how public prayer shapes urban identity, community cohesion, and intercultural dialogue, and assesses the long-term implications for social inclusion and civic pluralism. By situating Italy within the broader context of NDMCs, this study offers insights into how public religious practices function as symbolic instruments, negotiating visibility, legitimacy, and coexistence in contemporary multicultural societies.

title: Are you Listening to the Cackling or Counting the Eggs?
affiliations: University of Portsmouth

detail.title: Are you Listening to the Cackling or Counting the Eggs?
detail.abstract: Every leader professes a belief in meritocracy. Yet, in organizations worldwide, a silent, systemic bias is undermining this core principle, leading to strategic missteps and costly talent drain. We call this the Visibility-Performance Paradox: the pervasive tendency of organizational systems to reward employees for their visibility and self-promotion rather than their substantive contributions. The problem is captured in a classic management fable: A hen loudly cackles after laying a single egg, drawing the farmer’s attention and reward. Meanwhile, a codfish lays millions of eggs in complete silence, receiving no recognition. In our workplaces, the "hens"—employees skilled at impression management—are often celebrated, while the "codfish"—the quiet, consistent high-performers—are overlooked, become disengaged, and eventually leave. This isn't merely a matter of poor managerial judgment. Our synthesis of research on cognitive bias and motivation reveals it to be a baked-in systemic flaw. The good news is that by understanding its mechanics, leaders can build a culture that truly values substance over noise.

title: The Growing Role of NGOs in Shaping Global Diplomacy: Strategies and Impact on Transnational Issues
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: The Growing Role of NGOs in Shaping Global Diplomacy: Strategies and Impact on Transnational Issues
detail.abstract: Non-governmental organizations (NGOs) have emerged as pivotal actors in international relations, fundamentally altering the landscape of traditional state-centric diplomacy. This study analyzes the evolving role of NGOs in shaping global diplomacy by examining their strategies, effectiveness, and the challenges they face in addressing complex transnational issues. Employing a qualitative, comparative case study methodology, the paper focuses on two prominent examples operating in distinct sectors: Amnesty International in the field of human rights and Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) in global health. Key findings indicate that NGOs function as critical mediators that bridge the gap between civil society and governments, and as innovators that introduce novel solutions to complex problems. The study reveals significant strategic divergence, with human rights advocacy relying heavily on norm-setting and lobbying, while global health diplomacy prioritizes operational capacity and rapid crisis response. The paper concludes that while structural barriers such as limited formal authority and resource constraints persist, the effectiveness of global governance can be significantly enhanced by formalizing the role of NGOs in multilateral processes and fostering stronger cross-sector partnerships, thereby providing actionable recommendations for both policymakers and NGOs to amplify their collective impact.

title: Can Singapore's "Make Healthy Cheaper, Unhealthy Costlier" Approach Work in India?
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Can Singapore's "Make Healthy Cheaper, Unhealthy Costlier" Approach Work in India?
detail.abstract: Singapore's food policy framework blends behavioral science with fiscal design: make nutritious foods affordable and visible, while making high-sugar, high-fat options costlier and less accessible. This paper examines whether India can adapt this model. Drawing from case studies in Singapore, Mexico, the UK, Hungary, and Denmark, it explores policy levers, governance requirements, and socioeconomic trade-offs. Findings suggest that an India-fit combination of front-of-pack labeling, sugar-tiered excise taxes, and subsidies for healthy staples-rolled out through state-level pilots-could shift consumer behavior without disproportionate burden on low-income households.

title: Detecting Stablecoin Failure with Simple Thresholds and Panel Binary Models: The Pivotal Role of Lagged Market Capitalization and Volatility
affiliations: Moscow State University

detail.title: Detecting Stablecoin Failure with Simple Thresholds and Panel Binary Models: The Pivotal Role of Lagged Market Capitalization and Volatility
detail.abstract: In this study, we extend research on stablecoin credit risk by introducing a novel rule-of-thumb approach to determine whether a stablecoin is "dead" or "alive" based on a simple price threshold. Using a comprehensive dataset of 98 stablecoins, we classify a coin as failed if its price falls below a predefined threshold (e.g., $0.80), validated through sensitivity analysis against established benchmarks such as CoinMarketCap delistings and [Feder et al., 2018] methodology. We employ a wide range of panel binary models to forecast stablecoins' probabilities of default (PDs), incorporating stablecoin-specific regressors. Our findings indicate that panel Cauchit models with fixed effects outperform other models across different definitions of stablecoin failure, while lagged average monthly market capitalization and lagged stablecoin volatility emerge as the most significant predictors-outweighing macroeconomic and policy-related variables. Random forest models complement our analysis, confirming the robustness of these key drivers. This approach not only enhances the predictive accuracy of stablecoin PDs but also provides a practical, interpretable framework for regulators and investors to assess stablecoin stability based on credit risk dynamics.

title: Walking the Talk? Green Politicians and Pollution Patterns
affiliations: Halle Institute for Economic Research and European Central Bank (ECB)

detail.title: Walking the Talk? Green Politicians and Pollution Patterns
detail.abstract: Exploiting three decades of detailed regional data for Germany, we find that when the Green Party is successful at the polls, local hazardous emissions decline. The level of political representation matters, too. Green politicians’ gaining influence at county level is followed largely by a decline in air pollutants that have an immediate adverse health effect. In contrast, when the Green party joins the state government, only greenhouse gas emissions that affect the welfare of future generations via climate change decline. The primary mechanism to achieve lower emissions appears to be a reduction in output, rather than more efficient energy use.

title: Open Defecation Is Negatively Associated with Reported COVID-19 Deaths in Rural India. Are Shared Toilets the Reason?
affiliations: University of Washington - Economics, University of Washington and University of Minnesota - Minneapolis

detail.title: Open Defecation Is Negatively Associated with Reported COVID-19 Deaths in Rural India. Are Shared Toilets the Reason?

publicationDetails.journalName: IZA Institute of Labor Economics Discussion Paper Series

detail.abstract: Early in the COVID-19 pandemic, scientists and policymakers advocated for the reduction of open defecation to curb the diseases spread. However, SARS-CoV-2 is an airborne pathogen that can be transmitted by fecal aerosols, making poorly ventilated shared latrines a potential risk factor. Consequently, open defecation may mitigate COVID-19 transmission. Our study shows that reported COVID-19 deaths in India are negatively, rather than positively, correlated with district-level open defecation rates in rural areas. We also show that access to private toilets is associated with reduced individual-level mortality during the pandemic, but shared toilets do not show the same protective effect. Our results suggest that as with other diseases, private toilets reduce COVID-19 mortality, but the role of shared toilets and open defecation in relation to COVID-19 specifically is more nuanced. More broadly, our results show that public health measures must be targeted to the specific disease in question: what works for one disease may fail or even backfire when applied to others.

title: Teaching the Machine to Care A Field Guide to Ethical Intelligence in Education

detail.title: Teaching the Machine to Care A Field Guide to Ethical Intelligence in Education
detail.abstract:
The Challenge: The increasing acceleration of generative AI into daily life and classrooms has created a crisis of human coherence and trust. When technology evolves faster than human emotional and ethical understanding, fear and mental fragmentation—or metacognitive offloading—are the result.

The Solution: This guide, the practical companion to the research report The 5R Framework: Building Ethical AI Education for Human Flourishing, provides the emotional architecture of daily life necessary for navigating the AI age. It introduces Resonant Intelligence—a definition of technology as a mirror that learns from human tone and ethical rhythm—and translates the rigorous 5R Framework into immediate, personal practice.

The Practice: Through simple, no-equipment practices (Regulation, Reflection, Reasoning, Reciprocity, and Resonance), this book teaches students, teachers, and leaders how to:

  • Regulate the nervous system to remain calm amid digital chaos.

  • Reflect on internal motivation to defeat metacognitive offloading.

  • Reason with empathy to build truth-literacy and coherence.

This is a manual for strengthening the human curriculum of judgment, presence, and care, ensuring that consciousness remains the final arbiter of technology's purpose.

title: Mechanisms for Including Publics in Administrative Governance
affiliations: Georgetown University Law Center, Georgetown University Law Center, Georgetown University - Communication, Culture, and Technology Program and Georgetown University Law Center

detail.title: Mechanisms for Including Publics in Administrative Governance

declarations.funderStatement: This work was developed with the support of the Tech & Public Policy program at the McCourt School of Public Policy at Georgetown University, the Fritz Family Fellowship at Georgetown University, the Ford Foundation, and the Economic Security Project

detail.abstract:
The administrative state is struggling to counter the growing harms of the information economy. As we have documented in previous reports, existing regulatory tools were designed for an earlier era and are ill-suited to confront information-era harms such as algorithmic discrimination or AI-enabled manipulation. This document is part of a broader effort to rethink the role of the administrative state in governing a digital, data-driven economy. It explores methods for generating and mobilizing public participation–a longstanding pillar of administrative governance. 

Public participation in administrative processes serves several recognized purposes: it enhances the legitimacy of agency actions, helps guard against regulatory capture, and improves policy outcomes by surfacing a range of expertise and experience. Participation mechanisms are designed, at least in theory, to enable those affected by regulations to influence their development. In practice, however, it is often difficult for members of the public to meaningfully engage with agencies due to procedures that are opaque, outdated, and influenced by entrenched interests. For many, it is unclear whether participation would have any real impact at all. 

In this report, we develop a set of principles to guide the redesign of public participation mechanisms. These include: front-loading public engagement so that publics are involved sooner, building public capacity to enable meaningful engagement, building regulatory capacity to generate ongoing, two-way communication between regulators and publics, and reframing expertise as a public good to help facilitate informed contestation of policy priorities. 

Next, we propose specific mechanisms to facilitate the creation of information pipelines that are optimized for the timely transmission of two-way flows of high-quality, context-rich information between agencies and publics. Agencies must actively generate community engagement, gather community information, and facilitate structured deliberation and decision-making on issues central to the substance and design of regulatory oversight. 

Last, we propose recommendations for institutional redesign to embed participation mechanisms throughout the regulatory lifecycle. Public participation should begin at the agenda setting stage and extend through regulatory monitoring and enforcement of public mandates. Implementing these changes requires both appropriate resource allocation and some reorganization of internal agency processes.

title: In Search for the Optimal Law Governing Digital Payment Rights
affiliations: University of Arizona - James E. Rogers College of Law

detail.title: In Search for the Optimal Law Governing Digital Payment Rights
detail.abstract: This Article analyzes and contrasts three approaches to the financing of payment rights powering trade: (i) recognizing a digital equivalent of the paper document embodying the payment right, (ii) relying on an existing framework underpinning accounts receivable finance, and (iii) providing for a new digital asset embodying payment rights. Many questions abound. For instance, should the law simply recognize digital equivalents of negotiable instruments as devised for commercial practices of the 18th century, or cloak them with new features and functions suitable for the digital economy of the 21st century? How should the law governing assignments of receivables be modernized? Should multiple forms of payment rights that perform the same function be recognized? Legislative approaches must also consider technological aspects of issuing, holding, and transferring digital payment rights, which may be recorded in centralized registries maintained by public authorities or reflected in distributed ledgers maintained by no single entity.

title: Adapting the Navier-Stokes Equations to Economic Systems: A Dynamic Approach to Macroeconomic and Global Interactions
affiliations: Comillas Pontifical University - Faculty of Economics and Business Administration

detail.title: Adapting the Navier-Stokes Equations to Economic Systems: A Dynamic Approach to Macroeconomic and Global Interactions
detail.abstract: This paper develops a systematic adaptation of the Navier-Stokes equations-the central mathematical framework of fluid dynamics-to the analysis of economic systems, including macroeconomic dynamics, international trade, and spatially distributed interactions. We formalize a mapping between physical variables (velocity, pressure, density, viscosity, external forces) and economic variables (flows of capital and goods, price gradients, resource density, institutional frictions, policy and geopolitical shocks). Starting from the continuous Navier-Stokes system, we derive a discrete-time and discrete-space formulation suitable for macroeconomic modeling, global trade networks, and regional growth. We provide a detailed mathematical interpretation of each term in economic language. We then present numerical examples calibrated to recent US-EU-China trade magnitudes, illustrating how tariff shocks and logistic disruptions can generate nonlinear adjustments and turbulence-like dynamics in international flows. Finally, we implement computational simulations in Python for (i) a three-region global trade network and (ii) a two-dimensional Navier-Stokes-type spatial model. The overall framework provides a mathematically rigorous and computationally implementable approach to studying dynamic global interactions and structural shocks in modern economic systems.

title: Analysis of the Bollinger bands and Ornstein-Uhlebeck Model Mean Reversion Trading Strategy in S&P 500 Equities

detail.title: Analysis of the Bollinger bands and Ornstein-Uhlebeck Model Mean Reversion Trading Strategy in S&P 500 Equities

declarations.funderStatement: This research did not receive any specific grant from funding agencies in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: This paper examines mean reversion in S&P 500 equities over the period of 2010 to 2024, integrating Bollinger Band trading signals with Ornstein-Uhlenbeck (OU) process estimation to identify statistically significant mean-reverting behavior while taking survivorship bias into account. While the in-sample period (2010-2017) is used to estimate OU parameters and segregate statistically significant mean-reverting tickers, the out-of-sample period(2018-2024) assesses the performance of the corresponding trading strategy. Stocks exhibiting significantly strong OU-mean reversion strategy-defined by positive reversion speed (θ > 0.03), average p-value < 0.2, and average half-life in [5, 200] trading days-deliver significant returns and risk-adjusted performance relative to market benchmarks. The hybrid framework's robustness and profitability are confirmed by performance evaluation using the Sharpe, Sortino, and Calmar ratios in conjunction with maximum drawdown. The persistence of mean reversion across market regimes is reaffirmed by robustness checks conducted across different look-back windows and Bollinger Band thresholds. All results are reported gross of transaction costs. This study contributes to the literature on mean reversion by integrating Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process estimation with Bollinger Band signals. The framework improves the detection of statistically significant meanreverting behavior while accounting for survivorship bias, providing a robust base for future research in market efficiency and quantitative trading design.

title: The Strategic U.S. Currency-Industrial Model (C-IM): A Structural Solution to Replace Sovereign Debt with Productive Equity
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: The Strategic U.S. Currency-Industrial Model (C-IM): A Structural Solution to Replace Sovereign Debt with Productive Equity
detail.abstract: This framework introduces a fundamental shift in U.S. economic strategy, substituting external debt-based funding with productive foreign equity. The model achieves four simultaneous objectives: 1) It generates massive capital inflow for domestic manufacturing without adding to the national debt. 2) It resolves the single greatest friction in global capital flow: the Forex Reserve Dilemma. 3) It manages the resulting domestic liquidity through a capacity-driven absorption model, utilizing a controlled, short-term inflationary impulse to spur immediate capital expenditure. This impulse is immediately contained by the Fed's existing toolkit and ultimately neutralizes itself by creating long-term supply capacity, pushing U.S. GDP growth beyond the current 2-3% constraint. 4) It reinforces global dollar supremacy by utilizing the resulting foreign currency holdings as a powerful geopolitical hedge.

title: Robust Covariance Estimators: A Path Towards Optimal Portfolio Construction
affiliations: , Credit Agricole Assurances and Credit Agricole Assurances

detail.title: Robust Covariance Estimators: A Path Towards Optimal Portfolio Construction
detail.abstract:
The accurate estimation of covariance matrices is essential to Modern Portfolio Theory. Yet, financial data's inherent noise and spurious correlations make traditional sample covariance matrices ill-conditioned and unsuitable for portfolio optimization, because of high turnover and suboptimal ex-ante allocations. This paper jointly evaluates six covariance estimators - sample covariance, Ledoit-Wolf shrinkage, Random-Matrix denoising, Factor model, Graphical Lasso and CovPRCV - focusing on their ability to improve matrix conditioning, identify true dependence relationships between assets, and obtain investable optimal ex-ante portfolio allocations. 

Using both historical and synthetic data, the performance of all six covariance estimators is compared through matrix stability metrics and portfolio optimization outcomes. Clear performance hierarchies appear: Graphical Lasso and CovPRCV consistently outperform other methods by effectively suppressing spurious correlations and lifting small eigenvalues, resulting in well-conditioned covariance matrices that enable more stable and realistic portfolio allocations - greater portfolio performance, lower portfolio risk, and lower turnover. Graphical Lasso produces the smoothest portfolio weights with minimal turnover, while CovPRCV achieves superior risk-adjusted returns with lower portfolio risk. Both methods significantly reduce the optimizer's sensitivity to noise, leading to fewer constraint hits and more investable portfolios. Additionally, factoring regime-aware information into covariance estimators provides incremental value, particularly for weaker estimators, though this benefit diminishes as estimator robustness increases. 

By demonstrating the superiority of robust covariance estimators like Graphical Lasso and CovPRCV, this paper provides a clear framework for enhancing portfolio optimization, and a structured overview of how covariance estimators impact optimal portfolio allocations. The results show that moving beyond the sample covariance matrix leads to significant improvements in both matrix conditioning and real-world investment performance.

title: Spousal Labor Response to Primary Income: Identification and Heterogeneity
affiliations: Seoul National University - School of Economics, Statistics Norway - Research Department and Federal Reserve Banks - Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond

detail.title: Spousal Labor Response to Primary Income: Identification and Heterogeneity

publicationDetails.detailsText: Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond Working Papers, volume 25, issue 13, 2025[10.21144/wp25-13]

publicationDetails.journalName: Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: We present a new estimate for the elasticity of spousal labor supply in response to changes in the primary worker's income, the so-called "added worker effect." By leveraging firm-side information of the primary worker as an instrument, we isolate income changes that are uncorrelated with the spouse's productivity, addressing endogeneity bias. We find an economically meaningful role for the spousal labor supply, especially among young households with limited financial assets. We construct a heterogeneous agent model consistent with the estimated spousal employment response to design a government transfer program that effectively mitigates the negative income shock.

title: The EU Solidarity Contribution and a More Proportional Alternative: A Study Under EU and International Investment Law
affiliations: Lazarski University and Copenhagen Business School - CBS Law

detail.title: The EU Solidarity Contribution and a More Proportional Alternative: A Study Under EU and International Investment Law
detail.abstract: This paper reviews the EU Solidarity Contribution that was recently introduced by the Council Regulation on Emergency Intervention to Address High Energy Prices and proposes a more proportional alternative. It is argued that the legitimacy of the EU Solidarity Contribution might be disputed. The role that Member States have played in driving up energy prices by filling their natural gas storages much more than the EU's filling trajectory prescribes raises questions as to whether the EU Solidarity Contribution could be in conflict with the proportionality principle and whether all formal requirements of Article 122(1) Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU) have been fulfilled. Furthermore, it is argued that the EU Solidarity Contribution may compromise protection of investments under international investment agreements (IIAs) as the current design might entail elements that violate fair and equitable treatment (FET). As an alternative to the EU Solidarity Contribution, the article proposes the following. First, a legal commitment should be introduced for fossil fuel companies to invest 100% of their realized excess profit for decarbonizing the economy under the threat of taxing away those excess profits in their entirety should it become apparent that the investments are not actually realized. Second, in lieu of the EU Solidarity Contribution, the incidental financial support measures for vulnerable households could be financed with the excess (windfall) revenue collected from Value Added Tax (VAT) and excise due to the high inflation in the EU in 2022.

title: Leveraging Informality: Nigeria’s Uncut Gem to Leapfrogging Transformation
affiliations: Nigerian Economic Summit Group

detail.title: Leveraging Informality: Nigeria’s Uncut Gem to Leapfrogging Transformation
detail.abstract: The informal economy in Nigeria, often perceived as a developmental bottleneck, in fact represents the dominant logic of economic organisation in the country. With over 97 percent of businesses operating informally and accounting for more than 93 percent of employment, yet contributing disproportionately less to GDP, Nigeria's informality paradox presents both a structural challenge and a latent opportunity for economic transformation. This article contends that informality is not a transitory stage on the road to modern capitalism but a foundational economic reality embedded in the institutional, cultural, and entrepreneurial fabric of the Nigerian economy. Drawing on empirical data and theoretical insights, the article critiques prevailing formalisation-centric development paradigms and instead advances an informality-led transformation approach. This article emphasises the co-evolutionary relationship between informal and formal economic logics, highlighting how productivity-enhancing interventions, such as finance, infrastructure, digital tools, and policy innovation, can unlock the growth potential of informal enterprises and facilitate organic transitions to formality. By reframing informality as an endogenous asset rather than a liability, this article provides a new blueprint for inclusive and contextually grounded economic policy. It concludes by outlining strategic priorities that can reposition Nigeria's informal economy as a springboard for structural transformation and sustainable development.

title: Market Efficiency in the Digital Asset Token Ecosystem: A Tale of Originals, Operators, and Imitators
affiliations: Marquette University

detail.title: Market Efficiency in the Digital Asset Token Ecosystem: A Tale of Originals, Operators, and Imitators
detail.abstract: The emergence of Digital Asset Tokens (DATs), which are publicly traded equities representing claims on cryptocurrency assets, presents a novel setting to test the Efficient Market Hypothesis (EMH). This study introduces a three-category framework, classifying DATs as "Classic DAT" (Strategy, formerly MicroStrategy), "Miners" (cash-flow Bitcoin generators), and "The Imitators" (micro-cap strategic pivots using in-kind tokens). Analyzing daily returns from October 2023 to November 2025 (n = 554), we find a dramatic performance divergence irreconcilable with uniform market efficiency. "The Classic DAT" and "Miners" delivered strong, risk-adjusted returns during the crypto bull market, suggesting efficient pricing. Conversely, "The Imitators" suffered catastrophic capital destruction (-86.9% total return, Sharpe ratio =-0.423), indicative of profound and persistent mispricing. We attribute this inefficiency to narrative-driven overvaluation, information asymmetry, and behavioral biases. The results support a contextdependent view of market efficiency, where established business models are priced efficiently while complex, imitative financial innovations are not.

title: Confusion in the Judicial Review of Board Decisions to Remove Directors Under Section 71 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008
affiliations: University of South Africa

detail.title: Confusion in the Judicial Review of Board Decisions to Remove Directors Under Section 71 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008

keywords: Removal of directors by the board of directors
Section 71(5) of the Companies Act 71 of 2008
Judicial review of board decisions to remove a director
Awarding of costs in a section 71(5) review application

detail.abstract: A significant innovation of the Companies Act 71 of 2008, contained in section 71(3), is that the board of directors of companies is empowered to remove directors from office. Within twenty business days directors so removed may apply to court under section 71(5) of the Companies Act to have the board's decision reviewed. Section 71(5) is an essential remedy for directors. More than ten years after the promulgation of the Companies Act South African courts are beginning to develop the jurisprudence on the interpretation of section 71(5). This article examines recent cases in which courts had to interpret section 71(5) of the Companies Act. It discusses the following issues that these cases canvassed: (i) whether the board's power to remove a director under section 71(3) of the Companies Act constitutes administrative action and whether the Promotion of Administrative Justice Act 3 of 2000 applies to the review of these decisions under section 71(5) of the Companies Act; (ii) the ambit of a section 71(5) review and whether courts may review both the procedural aspects and the merits of the board's decision; (iii) the trigger for the twenty-business-day period to run; (iv) whether a court may condone a section 71(5) review application brought after the twenty business days expire; and (v) the awarding of costs in a successful section 71(5) review. As this article shows, courts have disagreed with and contradicted one another on the correct interpretation of section 71(5). This disagreement has led to confusion in South African law regarding the judicial review of board decisions to remove directors. Keywords Company law; removal of directors by the board of directors; section 71(5) of the Companies Act 71 of 2008; judicial review of board decisions to remove a director; types of judicial review; awarding of costs in a section 71(5) review application.

title: Lender Stress Tests and Corporate Credit Ratings
affiliations: Peking University, Peking University - Guanghua School of Management and University of Iowa

detail.title: Lender Stress Tests and Corporate Credit Ratings
detail.abstract: This paper examines how credit rating agencies assess firms’ creditworthiness when the firms borrow from banks subject to stress tests. Using a stacked difference-in-differences design, we find that firms borrowing from stress-tested banks receive higher credit ratings. The effect is stronger when these lenders impose or amend more covenants, face greater pressure from stress tests, or when borrower firms are financially constrained or exhibit lower financial transparency. We also show that banks increase their monitoring after becoming subject to stress testing. Collectively, these findings suggest that credit rating agencies perceive enhanced bank monitoring as a positive signal when assessing firm creditworthiness. Overall, this study contributes to the literature on the external drivers of credit rating assessments and deepens the understanding of spillover effects from the banking sector to the bond market.

title: Breaking the Bond: The Effect of Banker Turnover on Municipal Bonds

detail.title: Breaking the Bond: The Effect of Banker Turnover on Municipal Bonds
detail.abstract: Does banker human capital create value beyond bank-level effects in bond underwriting? I assemble novel data on senior banker mobility in public finance and study whether municipal borrowers benefit from following their banker when she moves to a new institution. To isolate the value added by the banker, I exploit quasi-exogenous variation from the 2021 Texas underwriter ban, which forced several major banks to exit municipal underwriting. Many bankers subsequently moved, inducing some borrowers to follow them. Using an instrumental variables approach, I find that following a banker reduces yield spreads by 19.5 basis points, with larger gains for bankers with MBA degrees. Bankers add value not only through information production but, more importantly, through their investor networks. These results imply that for bond underwriting, informational capital and investor relationships are portable with bankers, not institutions, and suggest a non-neutral effect on issuers when bankers move.

title: Silence in Acceptance of Contracts: Indian Legal Perspective

detail.title: Silence in Acceptance of Contracts: Indian Legal Perspective
detail.abstract: One of the nation's earliest mercantile laws, the Indian Contract Act went into force on September 1st, 1872. This law offers rules that facilitate the organized and regulated creation and observance of contracts. The basis for the course of action to be followed in the event of any disputes resulting from the contracts is provided by these rules and regulations. With the exception of Jammu & Kashmir, the entire nation is covered by the 266 parts of the Act. According to the Section 2(h) of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, a contract is “an agreement enforceable by law”. It has two elements: (a) an agreement; (b) legal binding. An agreement is every promise or the set of promises. Offer and acceptance are two key principles of Indian Contract Act, 1872. The communication of acceptance either orally or writing is essential to form a binding agreement. This research studies whether silence can constitute acceptance under Indian Contract Law. Under the Indian Contract Act, 1872, acceptance must be absolute, unqualified, and clearly communicated. In the case of Felthouse v. Bindley , the court had said that silence does not  amount to assent. Under circumstances, where there is duty to speak, prior course of dealings, commercial practises silence may bind the parties together. This research paper investigates silence in acceptance as a Indian Legal Perspective.

title: School Starting Age and the Gender Pay Gap over the Life Cycle
affiliations: University of Erlangen-Nuremberg-Friedrich Alexander Universität Erlangen Nürnberg and

detail.title: School Starting Age and the Gender Pay Gap over the Life Cycle
detail.abstract: This paper replicates and extends the evidence on the lifetime effects of school starting age on earnings by Fredriksson and Öckert (2014) for Sweden. Using German data for individuals born between 1945 and 1965, we examine a more rigid system of ability tracking in secondary education, a potential driver of long-term effects. We confirm negligible effects of later school entry for men and positive effects for women. These gender differences arise despite similar effects on educational attainment. By unfolding the gender gaps over the lifecycle, assessing fertility decisions, and maternal employment around the first birth, we show that childbirth postponement and increased labor market attachment after the first birth seem to be plausible mechanisms.

title: American Society of Evidence-Based Policing Causal Inference Workshop (Presentation Slides)
affiliations: Claremont Colleges - Claremont Graduate University and

detail.title: American Society of Evidence-Based Policing Causal Inference Workshop (Presentation Slides)
detail.abstract: This workshop provides a focused, full-day review of essential econometric methods for drawing credible causal inferences in evidence-based policy and policing. The morning session establishes the foundation by reviewing Descriptive Statistics and Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) regression, addressing critical topics such as OLS properties (BLUE), endogeneity, and corrections for non-spherical errors. The core of the workshop then transitions to the Causal Inference Toolkit, comparing Randomized Controlled Trials (RCTs) with quasi-experimental designs, including Instrumental Variables (IV), Difference-in-Differences (DD), and Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD). The afternoon sessions delve into practical application, covering various techniques for Controlling for Observables, such as Propensity Score Matching, Synthetic Control Methods, and Fixed Effects panel data models. The day culminates in a detailed examination of the Difference-in-Differences framework, focusing on the critical Parallel Trends Assumption, validation using Event Study Design, and addressing complexities related to staggered rollouts. Participants will gain a robust understanding of the strengths, weaknesses, and appropriate application of modern causal methods for data-driven decision-making.

title: A Literature Review: What Do We Know About Small and Mid-sized Bank Failure Resolution?

detail.title: A Literature Review: What Do We Know About Small and Mid-sized Bank Failure Resolution?

declarations.ethicsApproval: No ethics approval or consent is required.
declarations.funderStatement: I have received no funding.

detail.abstract: During crisis periods, many small and mid-sized (including regional) banks fail. In aggregate, these bank failures have high fiscal costs and significant effects on local-and sometimes national-economies; they also involve meaningful effort by regulatory authorities (RAs). How should governments resolve these institutions? There is no simple answer, but the available evidence provides insights. I discuss resolution objectives and the tradeoffs that RAs are likely to face. I then summarize a broad spectrum of relevant literature, including the economic effects of bank failure, franchise resolution options, fiscal losses, fire sales, distressed asset sale strategies and other relevant topics. This review of the literature reveals fruitful areas for additional research.

title: Light after the darkness: Estimating the impact of power outages on subsequent solar installations
affiliations: Kyoto University and Graduate School of Economics, Kyoto University

detail.title: Light after the darkness: Estimating the impact of power outages on subsequent solar installations
detail.abstract: Unexpected shocks to the electricity supply can influence people’s decision to invest in renewable energy, particularly when these technologies serve as substitutes for backup power. This study investigates the impact of a large-scale power outage on subsequent photovoltaic (PV) installations and examines how households and firms evaluate the expected benefit of PV systems as an emergency power source. Using a doubly-robust difference-indifferences design, we exploit the 2018 Hokkaido Eastern Iburi Earthquake in Japan as a natural experiment to estimate the effect of the subsequent blackout on municipality-level PV installations. Our results show that the blackout significantly increased commercial PV installations but had no effect on residential installations. In particular, commercial PV capacity rose by 3.900 kW per 1,000 people per half-year following the blackout. Additional analysis suggests that the intermittent nature of solar power may limit the reliability of residential PV systems during emergencies, especially under adverse weather conditions. These findings highlight the need to address intermittency to enhance the role of PV systems as a resilient infrastructure.

title: Anchoring and Cost Vector Design in Discrete Choice Experiments Testing Rational Choice, Coherent Arbitrariness, and Discovered Preferences
affiliations: University of Warsaw, University of Warsaw, German Centre for Integrative Biodiversity Research (iDiv) Halle-Jena-Leipzig, University of Warsaw and University of Warsaw - Faculty of Economic Sciences

detail.title: Anchoring and Cost Vector Design in Discrete Choice Experiments Testing Rational Choice, Coherent Arbitrariness, and Discovered Preferences
detail.abstract: This study revisits and extends the discussion by Bateman et al. (2008) regarding potential deviations from Rational Choice Theory, focusing on two hypotheses – Coherent Arbitrariness (CAH) and Discovered Preferences (DPH) – and their manifestations in Discrete Choice Experiments (DCEs). Using data from 5,917 Polish respondents, we implemented multiple treatments varying the cost vector, choice set size, priming techniques, and the placement of a contingent valuation Willingness To Pay (WTP) question either before or after the DCE. Our findings show that the design of the cost vector systematically influences stated preferences and that attempts to mitigate this anchoring effect (e.g., by presenting an open-ended WTP question prior to the DCE) were unsuccessful. The persistence of cost vector effects over time aligns with CAH, while the lack of any discernible preference refinement challenges DPH. Further analyses reveal systematic variations in cost sensitivity and show that excluding respondents who violated the Weak and Strong Axioms of Revealed Preferences did not reduce cost vector effects. In light of these results, we recommend using diverse cost vectors to verify the robustness of DCE-based welfare estimates and call for further research into the broader impacts of heuristic behaviors in stated preference methods.

detail.abstract: Accessibility is an essential yet often overlooked pillar of open science. While The R Journal embodies the spirit of open source and open access, true openness must also include usability for all readers, including those with disabilities. This article outlines a roadmap for enhancing accessibility within The R Journal, from adopting semantic and screen-reader-friendly formats to promoting inclusive figure design and reproducible code practices. It highlights current challenges in document structure, color usage, and metadata, and proposes practical strategies such as accessible R Markdown templates, HTML publishing, and accessibility review checklists. By integrating these improvements, The R Journal can extend its commitment to opennessensuring that the tools, data, and knowledge it shares are not only free to access but also accessible to everyone.

title: A Theory of Corporate Greenwashing
affiliations: Northwestern University

detail.title: A Theory of Corporate Greenwashing
detail.abstract: This paper develops a simple framework for studying corporate greenwashing. We study a belief-based notion of greenwashing: A stakeholder (consumer or investor) is greenwashed if she overestimates the environmental/social quality of a product/firm. Both the methods and the severity of greenwashing are endogenous to the communication environment. As an application, we show that under voluntary disclosure silence can be an effective greenwashing strategy and we identify the factors driving its severity. This form of silent greenwashing contrasts with the standard view of greenwashing as a vocal attempt to mislead.

title: The U.S. Supreme Court Should Provide Guidance on Applying Loper Bright in the U.S. Supreme Court Patent Case of Lynk Labs

detail.title: The U.S. Supreme Court Should Provide Guidance on Applying Loper Bright in the U.S. Supreme Court Patent Case of Lynk Labs

detail.abstract: When the Court issued Loper Bright last year—formally overruling Chevron and instructing courts to interpret statutes independently—it reshaped administrative law. Yet what has followed is striking: nearly a year later, there are no meaningful Supreme Court decisions applying Loper Bright. Not one fully developed opinion shows how the doctrine functions in practice. Lower courts have offered only scattered, inconsistent interpretations—too few to provide the coherent guidance that judges, lawyers, agencies, and law professors now urgently need. In many district and appellate decisions, courts “apply” Loper Bright by simply quoting its rejection of deference, but without explaining how textual interpretation should proceed when statutory ambiguity arises. The result is doctrinal silence at the very moment the legal system needs clarity most.That silence is especially problematic for law students—the next generation of advocates and judges—who now study Loper Bright in theory but have virtually no real cases to examine in practice. It is equally challenging for professors teaching administrative law, legislation, and statutory interpretation. Without examples, we cannot show students how the post-Chevron world works. And practitioners advising clients on regulatory exposure or statutory compliance are left reading tea leaves rather than precedent.

title: SCOTUS Should Clarify in the Patent Case of Lynk Labs, Inc. v. Samsung Co. Ltd. How to Apply Loper Bright v. Raimondo
affiliations: Oklahoma City University - School of Law

detail.title: SCOTUS Should Clarify in the Patent Case of Lynk Labs, Inc. v. Samsung Co. Ltd. How to Apply Loper Bright v. Raimondo

declarations.funderStatement: None

detail.abstract: For the past five years, I have taught Legislation & Regulation at Oklahoma City University School of Law—a course at the crossroads of administrative law, statutory interpretation, and the legislative process. Each semester, my students and I return to a central inquiry: when, if ever, should courts defer to agency interpretations, and when must judges exercise their own independent judgment? That question has taken on new urgency in the wake of the Supreme Court’s recent restructuring of administrative law. When the Supreme Court issued Loper Bright Enterprises v. Raimondo last year—explicitly rejecting the Chevron doctrine and directing courts to interpret statutes independently—it marked a transformational moment in administrative law. But nearly a year later, the Court has provided almost no guidance on how Loper Bright should operate in practice. That silence leaves lower courts, practitioners, and legal educators without real examples to illuminate what judicial interpretation should look like in a post-Chevron world. That gap is what prompted me to submit an amicus brief in Lynk Labs, Inc. v. Samsung Co. Ltd., urging the Court to take the case. Although Lynk Labs emerges from the patent system, the question it raises is universal: may a court quietly bypass Loper Bright by adopting an agency’s policy preferences over the statute’s actual text?

detail.abstract: This chapter's main objective is to critically analyze the phenomenon of corruption in Africa, and in the process highlight some major cases of corruption in the continent, describe the evolutions of the phenomenon, as well as recommend some possible ways and mechanisms for fighting the menace. The study looks at figures from Transparency International and United Nations Human Development Index and juxtaposed them with the changing dynamics of corruption in Africa. The method of study is critical analysis of individual cases, Africa corruption ranking and reviews of relevant empirical literature dealing with corruption in Africa. The study also adopts phenomenology as a study tool. Thus, the study relied heavily on secondary sources of information. The summary of the findings of the chapter shows the problem of corruption in Africa as endemic; something that has entered all the major sectors of modern African society.

title: Liquidation Shocks and Transaction Costs
affiliations: Pohang University of Science and Technology (POSTECH), Pohang University of Science and Technology (POSTECH) - Department of Industrial and Management Engineering and Pohang University of Science and Technology (POSTECH)

detail.title: Liquidation Shocks and Transaction Costs

declarations.funderStatement: NRF of Korea

detail.abstract: This paper analyzes an Epstein-Zin investor's consumption and portfolio-choice problem with proportional transaction costs and unhedgeable liquidation shocks, solving the resulting free-boundary system numerically. Our contribution is empirical and conceptual: introducing jump-driven forced-liquidation into a recursive-preference setting yields that liquidation risk can be an explaining factor for liquidity premia. Numerically, we check the effect of liquidation shock in both asset pricing perspective and trading frequency measure. Firstly, annual liquidation shocks raise the liquidity-premium-to-transaction-cost (LPTC) ratio substantially and cause the LPTC ratio to diverge near the no-trade boundaries; expected lifetime discounted transaction costs (EDTCs) increase with the liquidity ratio and are markedly larger with jumps. Also, the steady-state distribution shifts left, flattens, and concentrates mass nearer buy regions, implying that risk-averse investors may "buy more, sell less" to self-insure against forced liquidation.

title:
Digital Life of Russian Cities
Long-Term Dynamics
affiliations: SKOLKOVO Moscow School of Management - SKOLKOVO Institute for Emerging Market Studies, SKOLKOVO Moscow School of Management and SKOLKOVO Moscow School of Management

detail.title:
Digital Life of Russian Cities
Long-Term Dynamics
detail.abstract:
The issue of the digital divide, which emerged in the literature in the late 1990s, remains relevant today, especially in light of the "digital acceleration" brought about by the COVID-19 pandemic. Differences in access to digital technologies, their usage patterns, necessary skills, and resulting effects are dynamically evolving, taking on new forms and dimensions. This paper continues research on the second-level digital divide between Russian regions that was started in 2014, based on the "Digital Life Index," which compares digital demand and supply across seven dimensions of urban life based on "hard" statistical data on technology adoption. Since 2018, the study has covered over 90 Russian cities. A new wave of measurements conducted in 2023 allows for statistically sound conclusions about the dynamics of the digital divide in Russia, which are significant both theoretically and practically.
Over the five years between the two measurement waves, substantial investments were made under the national "Digital Economy" project and regional development strategies. As a result, more than half of the top-performing cities have changed, with many making leaps of dozens of positions. The COVID-19 pandemic significantly reshaped the structure of digital demand, while digital supply developed through incremental quantitative growth. Demand for digital services is rising across all sectors, yet their supply generally remains insufficient. This has exacerbated the mismatch between demand and supply and increased regional disparities. An analysis of the factors behind the digital divide shows —as in 2018—that it is not linked to regional income levels; instead, regional digital policies and the quality of human capital play a key role.  Thus, to reduce the digital divide, regional administrations should create conditions for private-sector participation in digital initiatives, leverage public-private partnerships for more efficient resource allocation, and develop and retain human capital through educational programs, awareness campaigns, and improved quality of life.

title: Mapping Work Flexibility in Europe: A Multidimensional Assessment
affiliations: , Independent and University of Bergamo - University of Bergamo,

detail.title: Mapping Work Flexibility in Europe: A Multidimensional Assessment
detail.abstract: This study examines the complex and multidimensional nature of work flexibility in Europe from the perspective of workers, with the aim of providing a comprehensive analysis of its determinants and implications. To this end, the research develops a composite indicator based on a novel theoretical framework that integrates multiple dimensions of work flexibility, which have not been previously combined in the existing literature. The analysis is structured around seven key pillars, including part-time employment, location flexibility, irregular and unconventional working hours, and work-life balance. The study utilised data from the European Working Conditions Survey for the years 2015 and 2021 and employed two distinct aggregation methods to construct the composite indicator. These included two noncompensatory methods, the adjusted Mazziotta-Pareto index and the geometric mean. The findings indicate that the geometric mean is the most robust and sensitive among the evaluated methods. Furthermore, the study emphasises that location flexibility is the most significant factor determining work flexibility across diverse national contexts. By bridging theoretical perspectives with empirical analysis, this study contributes to the understanding of the evolving nature of work flexibility and provides a methodological tool for its measurement. The findings offer valuable insights for policymakers and organisations seeking to enhance workplace adaptability in response to changing labour market conditions.

title: The Correlation Between Some Macroeconomic Indicators (Innovation, R&D, FDI) And Their Impact on the Increase of Labor Productivity

detail.title: The Correlation Between Some Macroeconomic Indicators (Innovation, R&D, FDI) And Their Impact on the Increase of Labor Productivity
detail.abstract: The objective of this study is to investigate the correlation between some macroeconomic indicators for labor productivity growth. In conditions of the current metamorphosis of the national economy, the identification of factors that contribute to the increase of labor productivity becomes a necessity for the survival of countries on the regional and world scale. The knowledge about these factors and their strategic combination contribute to the increase of productivity, of innovative business, which directly leads to the enhancement of well-being in the world economy. Economic growth in the countries of the world is directly proportional to the labor productivity equation, which is dependent on the number of unknowns expressed by its determinants. From this perspective, the author addresses the aspect of economic growth and the heterogeneity of the factors of increasing labor productivity in both national and global economies using the statistical method of correlating factors. The results of the study showed that investment, export, research, and development are factors that have a direct impact on economic growth, thus being possible to establish the strategies that are effective in the development of various national economies.

detail.title: Risk Management of Talent' Migration and Diaspora Inclusion in the Republic of Moldova and Bosnia and Herzegovina
detail.abstract: Introduction: Due to Globalization, worldwide migration has become a prominent phenomenon in the last decades, with the establishment of GATT and free movement rights. Aim: The main purpose of this research is to analyze the effect of brain drain, being a major risk for small countries with an economy in development, such as the Republic of Moldova and Bosnia and Herzegovina. Method: We utilize both national and international migration statistics portals to provide a better understanding of the historical and current trends. Moreover, we employ a theoretical framework to list some policies, developed by the national governments of the selected countries, with the aim to mitigate the risk of talent emigration. Findings: Most studies demonstrate the importance of diaspora engagement as a solution to the problem of brain drain. We identify some national governmental policies aiming to increase the level of collaboration between a state and its citizens outside the borders. Conclusion: The findings show the effective ways to support for sustainable development in the insurance sector. We can say the findings will be important data source for policy makers to make decisions. Originality and value: While in the past, brain drain became a problem for numerous states, brain gain is seen as a future economic driver. In that way, more interactive governmental policies should be created, aiming to foster a dynamic link between a skilled human force and the economy in development.

title: An Examination of the Revenue Sources and Expenditure Items of the EU Budget
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: An Examination of the Revenue Sources and Expenditure Items of the EU Budget
detail.abstract: The examination of this article is highly significant in terms of analyzing the EU budget system—recognized as one of the most successful union structures in the world—investigating how its revenues and expenditures are determined, and assessing the budgetary mechanism implemented in recent years. Since 1988, the Union’s budget, planned and executed for a seven-year period under the Multiannual Financial Framework, has been formed from various sources. While discussions on the Union’s seven-year budget begin three years prior to its entry into force, the Union’s annual budget is prepared through ten stages. The revenues of the EU budget consist of own resources such as the GNI-based contributions of member states, customs duties, plastic taxes, and VAT; moreover, as a result of recent global developments, revenue sources have been diversified. Expenditures are calculated before revenues, and it is of particular importance that expenditures are aligned with revenues and do not exceed them. The auditing of revenues and expenditures, as well as ensuring that they are carried out in accordance with established procedures, is conducted by the European Court of Auditors. In the budget calculated for the 2021–27 period, for the first time in EU history, Next Generation EU—i.e., borrowing—will be used as a revenue source. This resource will constitute nearly half of the budget, which exceeds 2 trillion euros. A large portion of the EU budget has long been financed by the so-called “Big Four” donors. Statistical indicators will be examined in greater detail in the article.

title: Sound Absorption Properties of Clay-based panels Mixed with Agro-industrial Residues of Crete
affiliations: , Technical University Of Crete, Technical University Of Crete, Technical University of Crete (TUC) - Department of Production Engineering and Management, Technical University Of Crete, Technical University Of Crete, Technical University Of Crete and Technology University of Braunschweig

detail.title: Sound Absorption Properties of Clay-based panels Mixed with Agro-industrial Residues of Crete
detail.abstract: The construction sector is a major source of environmental impact, generating over one-third of Europe's total waste, with limited progress in material reuse and substitution. In Mediterranean regions such as Crete, conventional construction materials-concrete, steel, and petroleum-based insulation-intensify ecological burdens and underscore the need for sustainable alternatives. This study investigates clay-based plasters and prefabricated panels enhanced with agro-industrial residues from Crete, including by-products from olive oil, citrus juice, and brewing industries. These residues, abundant and locally available, were integrated into clay mixtures to improve acoustic properties while promoting circular economy practices. Laboratory testings following ISO 10534-2 standard were conducted to measure normal-incidence sound absorption coefficient. The most important finding is that the increase in the proportion of barley in the samples results in a corresponding increase in the absorption coefficient across the entire measured frequency range. In contrast, no such increase is observed in the cases of olive and orange-hemp samples. The findings highlight the potential dual benefits of valorising waste streams and advancing low-carbon earthen construction techniques, offering building materials that support both sustainable waste management and improved indoor acoustic comfort.

title: The Great Resignation of the UK Labour Market
affiliations: University of Greenwich

detail.title: The Great Resignation of the UK Labour Market

declarations.declarationOfInterest: na
declarations.ethicsApproval: na
declarations.funderStatement: na

detail.abstract: This paper investigates whether the United Kingdom experienced a Great Resignation (GR) in the aftermath of the Covid-19 pandemic. Using Labour Force Survey (LFS) microdata, I complement aggregate labour-market indicators with individual-level probability models to analyse quitting behaviour, job-to-job (J2J) mobility, and associated wage outcomes. The results show that the UK's post-pandemic labour market was marked by a pronounced rise in quits and job moves between 2021Q3 and 2022Q4, consistent with a Great Resignation or Great Reallocation driven by workers transitioning into new jobs rather than exiting the labour force. The increase in mobility is more pronounced among younger, more educated, female, non-White, full-time, and permanent-contract workers, although most within-group differences are statistically small. While J2J transitions are associated with higher probabilities of wage gains, this relationship does not significantly strengthen during the GR period, suggesting a limited role of the GR in shaping post-pandemic wage dynamics. Moreover, there is little evidence of substantial sectoral or occupational reallocation. This study provides the first systematic evidence on the Great Resignation in the UK and contributes to the broader literature on post-pandemic labour-market adjustment.

title:
Is High Liquidity Always High?

Algorithms and the Endless Pursuit of Liquidity Patterns in the European Carbon Market
affiliations: Audencia Nantes School of Management and Audencia Business School

detail.title:
Is High Liquidity Always High?

Algorithms and the Endless Pursuit of Liquidity Patterns in the European Carbon Market
detail.abstract: This paper introduces a novel, relative liquidity measure, derived from the post-trade impact of observable market events, such as trades and orders. This is used to identify what level (threshold) of trading intensity is considered high, relative to prevailing market conditions. This is then used to investigate the reaction of algorithmic trading in the EU ETS to liquidity signals. The level of trading intensity (threshold) above which we observe more algorithmic trading is reversely proportional to trading activity, suggesting that algorithms become more "reactive" in more active market conditions. However, this threshold is elevated significantly after the introduction of the pre-and post-trade transparency requirements imposed by the MiFID II rules, implying that algorithms become systematically less "reactive" overall. This suggests that the major issue in carbon pricing in the EU ETS is not liquidity per se, but how it is related to signal clarity and, ultimately, to information diffusion.

title: Social Media Use and Psychosocial Implications of Covid-19 Pandemic among Adolescent Students

detail.abstract: COVID-19 has been an unexpected crisis period, directing the minds of people into ear and anxiety. Social distancing being a major preventive activity to overcome this contagious disease, which led to affect all aspects of life worldwide. Classroom learning has changed to virtual teaching during the lockdown period. A research was conducted to analyse the influence of COVID-19 on adolescents' social media usages. The study focused on social media usage and its impact on adolescents' psycho-social behaviour. Participants were 287 adolescent students from 6 mostly affected states of India. Data gathering was carried out during the COVID-19 Lockdown in India with a self-structured online questionnaire.Social media has helped them to cope with the isolated situation and has led to an increase in their creativity.
