Dysfunctional Poverty Causes Involuntary Unemployment and Disequilibrium

detail.abstract:
The separability rule is unable to distinguish between two commodities fulfilling the same need (multiplicative utilities) and their fulfilling different needs (additive utilities), if each utility specifies only diminishing marginal utility An S-shaped cardinal utility, bounded below and above, represents the individual’s experience of fulfilment of a need by a commodity – deprivation (increasing marginal utility (MU)), subsistence, sufficiency, and either satiation at finite consumption with the possibility of surfeit, or satiation at infinite consumption.
Functional forms are derived from a utility function for leisure and consumption, created by adding two normal cumulative distribution functions, with satiation at infinity, the parameters of each representing subsistence and intensity-of-need. The indifference curve map, demand and Engels curve diagrams are explored.

The main outcomes:
• Concave- (dysfunctional poverty) and convex-to-the-origin indifference curves are separated by a straight-line indifference curve, (an absolute poverty line), with slope defined by the relative-intensities-of-need.
• Budget movements on the indifference curve map reveal corner solutions and disequilibrium associated with dysfunctional poverty.
• The derived functional forms are functions of only the real wage rate and the endowment of unearned consumption.
• The derived functional form diagrams display: involuntary unemployment, disjointed curves, sticky wages and prices, wage- and price-elasticity associated with deprivation of a need, inferior normal and inferior-Giffen responses, and envelope curves.
• The co-incidence of the wage rate equalling the slope of the straight-line indifference curve and the endowment equalling its intercept, where both labour and consumption are very wage-, price- and endowment-elastic, leads to a highly unstable situation.

title: The Alwadhi Power-Law of Diamond Pricing: A Universal Mathematical Framework for Gemstone Valuation
affiliations: Maison Alwadhi ®

detail.title: The Alwadhi Power-Law of Diamond Pricing: A Universal Mathematical Framework for Gemstone Valuation
detail.abstract: We establish the first universal mathematical law for diamond pricing, addressing a fundamental gap in economic theory that has persisted since the formalization of commodity markets. The Alwadhi Power-Law states that diamond price scales with carat weight according to P=B ⋅W α ⋅C s ⋅∏ M q , where the critical exponent α=1.725 ± 0.012 emerges from the intersection of geological scarcity distributions, fractal formation processes, and market equilibrium dynamics. Through analysis of 1.2 million transaction records across global markets (2019-2024) and rigorous theoretical derivation from first principles, we demonstrate that this law represents a fundamental economic relationship analogous to gravity in physics or allometric scaling in biology. The power-law exponent sits precisely at the boundary between normal market behavior (α <2) and bubble dynamics (α >2), suggesting an efficient market equilibrium shaped by natural constraints. Empirical validation yields R 2 =0.9874 (p<10-15) with shape coefficients exhibiting remarkable stability across geographic markets (coefficient of variation ¿ 0.03). The law's mathematical structure enables closed-form solutions for derivative pricing, portfolio optimization, and risk assessment while maintaining computational efficiency three orders of magnitude superior to machine learning alternatives. This work not only provides the diamond industry with its first scientific pricing framework but also contributes to the broader understanding of power laws in economic systems, demonstrating how physical constraints and market forces combine to produce universal scaling relationships in commodity valuation.

title: Why Financial Governance Fails on Transportation Management

detail.title: Why Financial Governance Fails on Transportation Management
detail.abstract: This paper examines the global allocation of private capital between electric vehicles (EVs) and public transit, arguing that current investment patterns fundamentally undermine genuine decarbonization while espousing climate action rhetoric. Drawing on recent data (2021-2024) from BloombergNEF, the IEA, the ICCT, and the ITF, it is shown that while EVs can reduce emissions per vehicle, a universal rollout of private EVs would exceed the world's remaining carbon budget. Public transit, in contrast, delivers far higher energy, spatial, and material efficiency. The paper situates the cause of this mis-allocation within the structure of modern finance, traces this logical fallacy into the classrooms of the next generation of engineers and leaders, and concludes that only by staunchly rejecting this irrational approach and doing that which is necessary to redirect investment toward collective, electrified transit, can transport decarbonization remain compatible with a 2 °C world.

title: The Essence of Committed Leadership: Vision, Action, and Influence

detail.title: The Essence of Committed Leadership: Vision, Action, and Influence
detail.abstract: Committed leadership is a critical factor in driving organizational success, fostering team cohesion, and inspiring positive influence. This study explores the essential qualities that define a committed leader, emphasizing self-discipline, ethical integrity, vision, and the ability to inspire others. Drawing on the insights of renowned thought leaders such as Ray Kroc, John C. Maxwell, Abraham Lincoln, and John Wooden, it highlights five key dimensions of effective leadership: the standards leaders set for themselves, clarity of vision and example-based guidance, unwavering commitment to translating promises into results, willingness to prioritize collective goals over personal interests, and the capacity to influence and empower others. By examining these principles, the study underscores that leadership extends beyond formal titles or authority; it is manifested in action, consistency, and the transformative impact one leader can have on individuals and organizations. The findings provide a framework for understanding and cultivating leadership that is both principled and results-driven, offering practical insights for current and aspiring leaders seeking to create sustainable, positive change.

title: Globalization, Growth, and Energy Imports in Hungary: Implications for ESG and Sustainability Policy from a Threshold ARDL Analysis
affiliations: University of Pécs - Faculty of Business and Economics and University of Pécs

detail.title: Globalization, Growth, and Energy Imports in Hungary: Implications for ESG and Sustainability Policy from a Threshold ARDL Analysis
detail.abstract: As a post-transition economy, Hungary faces persistent challenges in reconciling economic growth with environmental sustainability amid the pressures of globalization and increasing energy dependence. While extensive research has explored the Environmental Kuznets Curve (EKC) and the environmental consequences of globalization, limited attention has been paid to the interaction between nonlinear growth dynamics and structural factors such as energy imports and European Union (EU) integration. This study addresses this gap by applying a multiple-threshold autoregressive distributed lag (MT-ARDL) model to assess the dynamic impacts of globalization, economic growth, and energy imports on Hungary's ecological footprint (EFP). Using annual data from 1970 to 2023, the analysis incorporates structural break unit root tests, threshold ARDL bounds testing, and frequency domain Granger causality to ensure methodological robustness. The findings indicate that environmental degradation is most severe during low-growth periods, whereas medium-and high-growth phases are associated with relative decoupling, driven by increased renewable energy use, improved energy efficiency and alignment with EU environmental regulations. Notably, energy imports aggravated environmental degradation during moderate growth but tended to mitigate ecological pressure under high-growth conditions, likely due to technological innovation and energy diversification. Globalization exerts a positive long-run influence by enhancing institutional quality and facilitating green technology transfer. These results have important implications for aligning Hungary's development trajectory with Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) objectives, highlighting the need for growth-sensitive 1 energy strategies, deeper regional integration, and strengthened climate governance to support a sustainable transition.

title: Monetary Policy and Anomalies
affiliations: CUNY Baruch College, Boston University - Questrom School of Business and Monash University - Department of Banking and Finance

detail.title: Monetary Policy and Anomalies
detail.abstract: We show that long-short anomaly portfolios exhibit significantly negative returns on monetary policy announcement days, in contrast to positive returns on other days. This effect is persistent and especially pronounced during periods of accommodative monetary policy. To quantitatively account for these findings, we develop a model in which monetary policy announcements reveal the Fed’s interest rate target, generating discount rate shocks. Heterogeneity in the sensitivity of stock valuations to these shocks gives rise to cross-sectional differences in announcement-day risk compensation. This sensitivity depends endogenously on anomaly signals: overpriced stocks have longer duration, are more exposed to interest rate risk, and therefore require higher expected returns than underpriced stocks. Lower interest rate environments reinforce this mechanism by increasing valuation sensitivity, leading to more negative anomaly portfolio returns.

title: Equivalence of Lindahl Prices and Core in a Collective Choice Problem
affiliations: Beijing Jiaotong University - School of Economics and Management

detail.title: Equivalence of Lindahl Prices and Core in a Collective Choice Problem

declarations.funderStatement: This research was supported by National Natural Science Foundation of China (Nos. 72271016 and 72571022), the Beijing Natural Science Foundation (No. Z220001).

detail.abstract: We study the collective choice problem examined by Delacrétaz et al. (2025), a framework that encompasses the allocation of both public and private goods as special cases and in which Lindahl prices are shown to exist and be efficient. We model the problem as a cooperative game and establish an equivalence between Lindahl prices and the core: every Lindahl price vector supports a core allocation, and every core allocation admits at least one corresponding Lindahl price vector. Moreover, distinct Lindahl prices supporting the same core allocation assign identical prices to all efficient alternatives. This result resembles a classical core-equivalence theorem but is derived without relying on replication or continuum-player settings. It further shows that, in collective choice problems, Lindahl prices are not only individually rational and socially efficient but also collectively rational. We also extend the single-firm setting in Delacrétaz et al. (2025) to a multi-firm setting and show that the equivalence between Lindahl prices and the core continues to hold. We further examine the connection between the VCG mechanism, prominent under incomplete information, and the core. We show that the core being a singleton is the necessary and sufficient condition for each of the following: (i) the VCG mechanism satisfies budget balance; and (ii) the VCG transfers lie in the core. This condition is shown to hold in shortage markets.

title: Beveridge Meets Phillips: Asset Pricing Implications *
affiliations: Xiamen University, Xiamen University and Institue for Financial and Accounting Studies, Xiamen University

detail.title: Beveridge Meets Phillips: Asset Pricing Implications *
detail.abstract: We extend a general equilibrium search model with labor heterogeneity and consumption price shocks for matching observed equity premium variability. We derive the labor market tightness factor from the Beveridge curve-the relationship between vacancies and unemployment-and derive the inflation factor from the Phillips curve-the association between unemployment and inflation-in explaining equity returns. A three-factor asset pricing model consisting of the market factor, the labor market tightness factor, and the inflation factor derived from this augmented search model captures large variations of stock returns in the cross-section. Agents demand negative risk premiums for labor market tightness via cash flow risks and positive premiums for the personal consumption expenditure index through discount rate risks.

title: A Mudskipper-Inspired Soft Robot for Precision Agriculture in Egypt's Northern Nile Delta

detail.title: A Mudskipper-Inspired Soft Robot for Precision Agriculture in Egypt's Northern Nile Delta
detail.abstract: Agriculture in Egypt’s Nile Delta is increasingly threatened by environmental stressors such as soil salinization, waterlogging, and pH imbalances, which significantly reduce crop productivity and impact food security (Elshaer et al., 2021; Hassan Mohamed, 2020). Conventional farming techniques and mechanized soil monitoring systems often prove ineffective in the swampy, salt-affected landscapes of the northern Delta (Abdel-Mottaleb et al., 2019). To address these challenges, this paper proposes a novel mudskipper-inspired soft robotic system that integrates biomimicry principles with IoT-enabled sensing technologies for real-time, minimally invasive soil condition monitoring and remediation. The robot’s soft, servo-actuated limbs enable adaptive locomotion across delicate crops and saturated soils without causing damage, while embedded sensors continuously measure salinity and pH levels to inform precision agriculture practices (Zhang et al., 2022). By providing accurate spatial and temporal soil data, this system supports targeted interventions to enhance soil fertility, increase agricultural yields, and promote sustainable livelihoods in vulnerable Nile Delta communities. The approach demonstrates the potential of soft robotics combined with environmental sensing to overcome limitations of traditional methods and offers a scalable solution for similar coastal agricultural regions facing climate-driven salinity challenges.

title: Breaking the Transactional Symmetry: Towards an Asymmetric Monetary Architecture for Regenerative Economies

detail.title: Breaking the Transactional Symmetry: Towards an Asymmetric Monetary Architecture for Regenerative Economies

declarations.funderStatement: This research received no dedicated funding beyond the ADEME “Low-Tech and Territorial Resilience” call for commons (2020).

detail.abstract: Our societies face a structural contradiction: every act of environmental sobriety or social care, vital for planetary limits and social foundations, is still recorded by our economic instruments as a loss of wealth. Current monetary systems, inherited from the Neolithic era, recognise only private value. Consequently, within transactions, the preservation of common goods (climate, biodiversity, social cohesion...) appears as a cost, never as a creation of wealth. This paper proposes a hypothesis for overcoming that accounting lock-in: the emergence of monetary systems able to recognise, within each transaction, the collective value created or destroyed. We name these currencies Common Good Units (UBiC for “Unité de Bien Commun” in french). Unlike conventional “private-good” currencies, UBiC intentionally break transactional symmetry: when an activity benefits the commons, new money is issued; when it harms them, money is destroyed. We outline the theoretical rationale, preliminary simulations, and research-action pathways for testing this hypothesis, addressing inflation control, convertibility, and banking compatibility. We invite the scientific community to investigate whether aligning private incentives with collective interests can, through the very architecture of money, render regenerative behaviours economically profitable.

title: Injury and Accountability in Cyberspace: Applying Lessig's Four-Restraints Framework to the Question of Mandatory Identity Disclosure in Ghana
affiliations: Public Relations Ghana

detail.title: Injury and Accountability in Cyberspace: Applying Lessig's Four-Restraints Framework to the Question of Mandatory Identity Disclosure in Ghana

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Not applicable.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable.
declarations.funderStatement: Not applicable.

detail.abstract: Ghana's 1992 Constitution guarantees the rights to privacy and free speech, both of which are vital for personal liberty and democratic participation. The Data Protection Act, 2012 (Act 843), reinforces these rights by safeguarding online identities, thereby fostering cyberspace anonymity. While anonymity protects privacy and encourages free expression, it also enables harmful conduct, including the dissemination of misinformation, cyberbullying, and other unlawful activities. Cyberlibertarians, such as John Perry Barlow, argue against all forms of governmental intervention in cyberspace; however, cyberpaternalists like Lawrence Lessig believe that the unique characteristics of the internet make it possible for the law to intervene. Using Lessig's four-restraints framework-law, markets, architecture, and norms-this paper analyses the tension between injury prevention and rights protection in Ghana's digital space. It concludes that a mandatory identity disclosure is not a necessary policy response to address cyberspace injury and accountability.

title: Large Moves in the Foreign Exchange Market
affiliations: University of Liverpool - Management School (ULMS), University of Cambridge - Judge Business School, University of Cambridge - Judge Business School and  Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)

detail.title: Large Moves in the Foreign Exchange Market
detail.abstract: The timing of large currency moves - say three-standard deviations events - is often considered random. In contrast, we show that a non-trivial proportion of large moves in exchange rates is predictable in real time via the slope of the term structure of option-implied volatility (IV). Specifically, the difference between short-term and longer-term IVs is a significant and robust predictor of large currency returns in absolute value. This predictive relationship is exploitable in a trading strategy that buys strangles when the term structure of IV is sufficiently inverted, to profit from the subsequent realization of such large moves.

title: Exploring the Tapestry of Tourism: A Comparative Study of a Selection of Balkan Countries
affiliations: University of Shkodra

detail.title: Exploring the Tapestry of Tourism: A Comparative Study of a Selection of Balkan Countries
detail.abstract: This study employs time series analysis to examine the factors influencing fluctuations in tourist arrivals within a certain timeframe (1993-2023) across a chosen set of Western Balkan nations. The countries that have been chosen for this study are Albania, Croatia, Montenegro, and Greece. These nations exhibit distinct attributes in terms of their socioeconomic development patterns; nonetheless, they share commonalities in terms of their coastal topography and cultural heritage influences. In this study, GMM models will be employed to analyze the relationship between the number of tourist arrivals and international tourism receipts. The models will incorporate various independent variables, including GDP growth rate, consumer price index, exchange rate, transportation costs, and other pertinent factors associated with tourism infrastructure. Based on our estimation results, we have observed small variations among countries, indicating a relatively low amount of price elasticity. Nevertheless, when considering Balkan countries, it is shown that income level and currency rates hold greater significance.

title: Leverage Volatility Risk *
affiliations: Xiamen University, Xiamen University and Institue for Financial and Accounting Studies, Xiamen University

detail.title: Leverage Volatility Risk *
detail.abstract: We show that time variations in intermediary leverage volatility affect asset prices. Leverage volatility is a negatively priced source of risk. At the firm level, exposure to leverage volatility risk inversely predicts future returns, yielding a spread across decile portfolios of 5.2 (4.4) percent annually when measuring intermediary leverage with security broker-dealer (primary-dealer) data. When leverage volatility is high in recessions, equity term premiums increase, and the intermediary expects low returns in the future, leading to negatively expected changes in equity yields. Thus, the slope of the equity yield curve is potentially negative in busts and vice versa.

title: The Supreme Court Should Clarify How to Apply Loper Bright in the Patent Law Case of Lynk Labs, Inc. v. Samsung Co. Ltd.
affiliations: Oklahoma City University - School of Law

detail.title: The Supreme Court Should Clarify How to Apply Loper Bright in the Patent Law Case of Lynk Labs, Inc. v. Samsung Co. Ltd.

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None
declarations.ethicsApproval: None
declarations.funderStatement: None

detail.abstract: When the Supreme Court issued Loper Bright Enterprises v. Raimondo last year-squarely rejecting Chevron and instructing courts to independently interpret statutes-it marked a watershed moment in administrative law. Yet nearly a year later, the Court has provided virtually no guidance on how Loper Bright should be applied. That silence leaves courts, practitioners, and those of us training future lawyers without real-world examples to illuminate this new interpretive landscape. That is why I submitted an amicus brief in Lynk Labs, Inc. v. Samsung Co. Ltd., urging the Court to grant review. Although the case arises in the patent arena, it presents a far more universal question: whether lower courts may quietly sidestep Loper Bright by elevating agency policy preferences over statutory text.

title: Pricing abnormal weather risks in Chinese stock market
affiliations: South China University of Technology and South China University of Technology

detail.title: Pricing abnormal weather risks in Chinese stock market
detail.abstract: We construct six monthly abnormal weather indicators by employing physical weather data of temperature, humidity, wind speed, precipitation, sunshine hours and sky coverage in China. We compute the abnormal weather betas to proxy for abnormal weather risks and investigate the pricing effects of these risks in the Chinese stock market. We find a low abnormal weather beta premium in the cross-section, i.e., stocks with high betas to changes in the abnormal weather index significantly underperform those with low betas by 0.13% to 0.57% per month on a risk-adjusted basis. In particular, the low abnormal weather beta premiums of temperature, sunshine hours, and sky coverage are significant over the subsequent six months. The further analyses suggest that the abnormal weather betas exhibit persistent long-term predictive power and have significant explanatory power for size, value, and long-term reversal anomalies.

title: A Review of Theoretical and Empirical Models of Sovereign Debt
affiliations: University of York

detail.title: A Review of Theoretical and Empirical Models of Sovereign Debt
detail.abstract: This paper investigates how unexpected US monetary policy shocks affect sovereign risk and macroeconomic dynamics in Latin American emerging markets, combining theoretical modelling and empirical analysis. I develop a two-period sovereign default model that incorporates domestic households, government borrowing, and default decisions under financial constraints. The model extends existing frameworks by introducing a dual liquidity structure and linking default probabilities endogenously to international interest rates, thereby capturing the transmission of external financial shocks. Within this framework, a contractionary US monetary policy shock raises sovereign risk, increases lending rates, reduces bank credit to the corporate sector, and ultimately depresses industrial production. Empirically, I employ the orthogonalized US monetary policy surprise measure as an exogenous variable in panel regressions and a dynamic panel model covering Brazil, Chile, and Colombia. Results show that tighter US monetary policy increases sovereign bond yield spreads, reduces government bond values, and adversely affects financial and macroeconomic conditions. Moreover, the analysis highlights the role of investor composition: greater foreign participation in domestic bond markets mitigates the spread response to monetary shocks, suggesting a stabilising effect of international investors. By integrating theoretical and empirical perspectives, this study contributes to the sovereign debt literature in two ways. First, it provides a structural explanation for the mechanisms through which global monetary tightening transmits to emerging markets. Second, it offers new evidence on the interaction between external shocks, sovereign risk, and financial frictions in Latin America, yielding relevant insights for policymakers concerned with financial stability and external vulnerability.

title: Towards Credible Corporate Net-Zero Commitments? On the Role of Unfair Commercial Practices Law in Contesting Global Value Chain Greenwashing
affiliations: Tilburg Law School

detail.title: Towards Credible Corporate Net-Zero Commitments? On the Role of Unfair Commercial Practices Law in Contesting Global Value Chain Greenwashing

declarations.funderStatement: I wish to acknowledge the funding provided for this project under the Incentive Grant Scheme of the Dutch Government 'Stimuleringsbeurs' for the project ‘Regulating Risk in the Age of Global Value Chains’. For more information, please visit (https://research.tilburguniversity.edu/en/persons/paul-verbruggen/projects/).

detail.abstract:
Corporate net-zero commitments are voluntary, forward-looking statements regarding a company's public commitment to reduce greenhouse gas emissions along its global value chain (GVC). These commitments are part of a wider set of strategies that aim at reducing the environmental impact of business operations in GVCs. Whether this particular strategy of greening GVCs can meet that goal fundamentally depends on the credibility of these commitments. Without it, critics say, the pledges amount to nothing less than corporate greenwashing. In this Chapter, I discuss the various credibility concerns of corporate net-zero commitments to identify and critically analyse the potential of unfair commercial practices laws to contest this form of GVC greenwashing. By focusing the analysis on the European legal framework, I demonstrate that such laws offer important relative benefits over other domains of private law in making the corporate commitments credible. They complement and reinforce other public and private regulatory efforts to ensure the adequacy and integrity of these pledges. Unfair commercial practices law therefore constitutes an important legal strategy for regulating sustainability in GVCs, one that corporations in the chain need to recon with when communicating net-zero targets to downstream market actors.

Forthcoming in: Debadatta Bose, Anne Lafarre, Ricardo Garcia Anton, Bas Rombouts and Paul Verbruggen (eds), Cambridge Handbook of Law and Responsible Business: Legal Strategies for Sustainability in Global Value Chains, Cambridge University Press 2026.

title: Automated Ball-Strike System(ABS) and Shift Ban: An Event Study Analysis of the 2024 KBO Rule Changes on Player Performance
affiliations: Dankook University and Pusan National University - Department of Economics

detail.title: Automated Ball-Strike System(ABS) and Shift Ban: An Event Study Analysis of the 2024 KBO Rule Changes on Player Performance
detail.abstract: This study investigates the causal impact of the 2024 rule changes in the Korea Baseball Organization (KBO)-specifically the introduction of the Automated Ball-Strike System (ABS) and the prohibition of defensive shifts-on batter performance. Using daily game log data from 2022 to 2025, we employ a fixed-effects model controlling for player, team, and seasonal seasonality to estimate the monthly effects of these policy interventions. Our event study results reveal a significant structural shift in plate discipline and outcomes. We find a robust "trade-off" effect: the implementation of ABS is associated with a statistically significant increase in strikeout rates (SO%) and a decrease in walk rates (BB%), suggesting a stricter and more consistent strike zone. However, despite the rise in strikeouts, overall batting averages (AVG) remained stable or increased, primarily driven by a rise in Batting Average on Balls In Play (BABIP) attributed to the defensive shift ban. Furthermore, we identify a pronounced lateseason surge in offensive metrics in the post-policy years, indicating an interaction between rule changes and pitcher fatigue in September and October.

title: Student Debt and the Cinderella Effect
affiliations: Pennsylvania State University - Department of Finance, Pennsylvania State University - Department of Finance, University of Calgary - Finance and

detail.title: Student Debt and the Cinderella Effect
detail.abstract: Unexpected intercollegiate athletic success generates a variety of changes at universities -- including increased salience and status of sports-oriented activities among students, known colloquially as the "Cinderella effect". By linking data on athletic contest outcomes, betting lines, student debt default rates, and post-college earnings data, we find that Cinderella events disrupt human capital development among incumbent students and adversely affect their financial outcomes. Following such events, treated students exhibit higher default rates and lower earnings. This effect strengthens with treatment exposure (results are larger for freshmen than seniors) and is concentrated in low-ranked universities. These institutions show no changes in revenues or expenditures, suggesting that resource-driven explanations are unlikely to be the primary driver. In contrast, students at high-ranked universities have marginally lower default rates and higher earnings, as these schools receive more applications, increase selectivity, and have marginally higher revenues and expenditures. Overall, our results suggest that athletic success shifts students' preferences away from academic focus. More broadly, our results show that university environment affects human capital development, as distinct from selection effects that reflect assortive matching between students and universities.

title: Corporate cybersecurity risk and economic policy uncertainty: Insights from textual analysis and board governance
affiliations: NIDA Business School, National Institute of Development Administration (NIDA), Pennsylvania State University - School of Graduate Professional Studies (SGPS), Sasin GIBA, Mahidol University International College (MUIC) and Central Washington University

detail.title: Corporate cybersecurity risk and economic policy uncertainty: Insights from textual analysis and board governance

keywords.keywords: Cybersecurity riskEconomic policy uncertaintyCorporate governanceRisk disclosureEnterprise risk management

detail.abstract: This study examines how firms adjust their cybersecurity risk exposure in response to economic policy uncertainty (EPU). Using a text-based measure of firm-specific cybersecurity risk from annual risk-factor disclosures and more than 35,000 firm-year observations, we test two competing perspectives: the vulnerability hypothesis—where higher EPU constrains cybersecurity investment—and the vigilance hypothesis—where uncertainty heightens risk-mitigation efforts. The evidence supports vigilance. A one-standard-deviation increase in EPU is associated with a 10.3% reduction in reported cybersecurity risk exposure, robust to propensity score matching, entropy balancing, and instrumental-variable estimation. Governance also moderates this relationship: firms with more independent and gender-diverse boards exhibit a weaker decline in cybersecurity risk during periods of heightened uncertainty. Our findings contribute to research on risk disclosure and corporate governance by showing how policy uncertainty shapes cybersecurity oversight, with implications for regulators, boards, and policymakers focused on enterprise risk management and cyber resilience.

title: Immigrants, Imports, and Welfare: Evidence from Household Purchase Data
affiliations: , University of Toronto and

detail.title: Immigrants, Imports, and Welfare: Evidence from Household Purchase Data
detail.abstract: Who buys imports? By augmenting U.S. grocery purchase data to include origin countries of both products and households, we provide the first evidence that immigrants exhibit substantially stronger preferences for imported consumer goods than natives. We develop and estimate a quantitative trade model to show that immigrants also reduce trade costs and expand the effective market size for foreign goods, thereby increasing local import supply for all households. Overall, however, immigrants generate considerably more local import expenditure via their own purchases than via spillovers to natives, with profound implications for the distributional costs of a negative trade shock, such as an import tariff: the average within-county difference in welfare costs between immigrants and natives is over six times the across-county standard deviation in native household costs.

title: AI Images, Labels and News Demand
affiliations: WZB Berlin Social Science Center, University of Bath, University of Barcelona - Institut d'Economia de Barcelona (IEB) and

detail.title: AI Images, Labels and News Demand
detail.abstract: We test whether AI-generated news images affect outlet demand and trust. In a pre-registered experiment with 2,870 UK adults, the same article was paired with a wire-service photo (with/without credit) or a matched AI image (with/without label). Average newsletter demand changes little. Ex-post photo origin recollection is poor, and many believe even the real photo is synthetic. Beliefs drive behavior: thinking the image is AI cuts demand and perceived outlet quality by about 10 p.p., even when the photo is authentic; believing it is real has the opposite effect. Labels modestly reduce penalties but do little to correct mistaken attributions.

title: Non-Fundamental Expectations and Asset Growth Factor Timing
affiliations: Shanghai University of Finance and Economics and School of Finance, Shanghai University of Finance and Economics

detail.title: Non-Fundamental Expectations and Asset Growth Factor Timing
detail.abstract: This paper investigates the time variation in the returns to the asset growth (AG) factor by proposing two complementary predictors: the intangible and tangible spreads. These portfolio-level measures respectively capture the market's time-varying responses to non-fundamental and fundamental information regarding corporate investment. We find that only the intangible spread predicts future AG factor returns. Its predictive power persists after controlling for industry effects, other firm characteristics, and macroeconomic variables, and holds in out-of-sample tests. Using event-based analyses and analyst forecasts, we provide a mispricing-based interpretation: the intangible spread captures investors' time-varying extrapolation of non-fundamental information embedded in firms' investment decisions.

title: Pricing the Common Ground Taxonomy: Evidence from Corporate Green bonds
affiliations: Shanghai Dianji University, Central University of Finance and Economics and The University of Western Australia - UWA Business School

detail.title: Pricing the Common Ground Taxonomy: Evidence from Corporate Green bonds
detail.abstract: Common Ground Taxonomy (CGT) identifies the commonalities between EU’s Sustainable Finance Taxonomy and China’s Green Bond Endorsed Project Catalogue. We document that the yield spreads of CGT-labelled bonds are about 5.89 basis points lower than that of comparable non-CGT-labelled green bonds in China. The CGT premium is more pronounced when the green bonds are labelled at issuance. Further analyses show that the impact of CGT labelling on bond pricing is more pronounced when the issuers have lower ESG rating and more foreign institutional investors. In addition, we document that both the total amounts of subscription in the primary market and the liquidity in the secondary market are higher for CGT-labelled bonds compared with other green bonds.

title: Dilution vs. Risk Taking: Capital Gains Taxation and Entrepreneurship
affiliations: University of Pennsylvania - The Wharton School, University of Zurich, National Bureau of Economic Research (NBER), University of Pennsylvania - Business & Public Policy Department and Swiss Finance Institute - University of Zurich

detail.title: Dilution vs. Risk Taking: Capital Gains Taxation and Entrepreneurship
detail.abstract: Recent proposals to tax unrealized capital gains or wealth have sparked a debate about their impact on entrepreneurship. We show that accrual-based taxation creates two opposing effects: successful founders face greater dilution from advance tax payments, whereas unsuccessful founders receive tax credits that effectively provide insurance. Using comprehensive new data on U.S. venture capital deals, we find that founder returns remain extremely skewed, with 84% receiving zero exit value while the top 2% capture 80% of total value. Moving from current realization-based to accrual-based taxation would reduce founder ownership at exit by 25% on average but would also increase the fraction receiving positive payoffs from 16% to 47% when tax credits are refunded. Embedding these distributions in a dynamic career choice model, we find that founders with no or moderate risk aversion prefer the current realization-based tax system, while more risk-averse founders prefer accrual-based taxation. We estimate that a 2% annual wealth tax has a similar impact on dilution as taxing unrealized capital gains, but produces no risk-sharing benefits due to the absence of tax credits in case of down rounds.

title: TRENDS IN CHANGES IN THE RUSSIAN CORPORATE BOND MARKET
affiliations: The Russian Presidental Academy of National Economy and Public Administration, Noth-West Institute of Management, Russian Presidential Academy of National Economy & Public Administration and Russian Presidential Academy of National Economy & Public Administration

detail.title: TRENDS IN CHANGES IN THE RUSSIAN CORPORATE BOND MARKET
detail.abstract: Bonds are one of the key instruments of corporate financing, allowing companies to attract long-term capital on market terms. The article considers the essence and classification of bonds, their advantages and disadvantages, and analyzes the trends in the development of the corporate bond market in Russia. Having set the goal of identifying trends in changes in the Russian bond loan market under the influence of inflation, crises and sanctions, the authors examined statistical data of the financial market segment under study, determined cause-and-effect relationships between changes in the volumes and terms of borrowings, as well as the industry structure of this market segment. Particular attention is paid to the influence of macroeconomic conditions, interest rates, and government policy on the corporate bond market. The article will be of interest to private investors prone to moderate risk and a conservative investment strategy.

title: The Great Leveler According to HANK
affiliations: University Tuebingen, University of Tübingen - Department of Economics, University of Bonn and University of Bonn

detail.title: The Great Leveler According to HANK
detail.abstract: Using historical income and wealth data, we show that war reduces inequality: the top-1% income share falls by 20% and the top-1% wealth share by 10%. We measure three key drivers of inequality - capital destruction, taxation, and inflation - in the data and quantify their role with a Heterogeneous Agent New Keynesian (HANK) model. Destruction depresses profits and thus top incomes. Taxation primarily influences wealth dynamics, while inflation has little effect on top shares, but reduces indebtedness among poorer households. We validate our findings using new data on inequality across German towns in World War 2 and cross-country data on profits.

title: Balancing environment, production, profitability, planning, and trade: divergent perspectives on food preparedness in agriculture
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Independent, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences (SLU)

detail.title: Balancing environment, production, profitability, planning, and trade: divergent perspectives on food preparedness in agriculture
detail.abstract: Profitability and environmental sustainability have long been central to agri-food policy. New demands of building capacity of food supply in crises challenges agri-food system actors to step up the work on food preparedness. Understanding this shift requires exploring how stakeholders view sustainable preparedness. The aim of this study was to assess stakeholders’ perspectives on how they perceive the challenges and issues related to the role of Swedish agriculture to ensure supply of food commodities in times of crises. Using Q-methodology, 47 statements drawn from policy documents and media on food production, sustainability, and preparedness were sorted by 26 food chain actors in Sweden based on how closely each statement aligned with their individual perspectives. Seven interviews provided further clarification and interpretation of the results. Factor analysis identified four factors, including one bipolar factor, which we interpreted as five distinct perspectives: 1) “Act for a nature-based shift” is a perspective leaning on principles of environmental sustainability with an emphasis on low-input solutions. In opposition to the nature-based shift 2) “Strengthening current production” prioritizes domestic inputs and cattle production. 3) “Ensure long-term solutions” focuses on profitability and diversification of cropping systems. 4) “Go for contingency planning” and 5) “Keep up international trade” are two perspectives with a particular focus on food preparedness and they differ by the emphasis on trade in the latter. The findings reveal conflicting views among stakeholders, providing valuable insights to guide future research on how sustainable preparedness should be operationalized, implemented and monitored.

title: Six Pocket Syndrome Theory: A Comprehensive Analysis of Child Development and Parenting Practices in Contemporary India
affiliations: Azim Premji University

detail.title: Six Pocket Syndrome Theory: A Comprehensive Analysis of Child Development and Parenting Practices in Contemporary India

detail.abstract: Six Pocket Syndrome-excessive concentration of financial and emotional resources from six family members (two parents, four grandparents) toward a single child-has emerged as a critical concern in contemporary India due to rapid demographic transitions, urbanization, and changing family structures. The Total Fertility Rate decline from 3.4 (1992-93) to 2.0 (2019-21) mirrors demographic conditions conducive to syndrome development. A systematic literature review incorporating peer-reviewed research, demographic data, government policy analysis, and crosscultural comparative studies spanning 2011-2025 was conducted across academic databases (Google Scholar, PubMed, JSTOR). The analysis integrated insights from developmental psychology, family systems theory, and sociocultural research to examine prevalence, manifestation patterns, developmental impacts, and intervention strategies. Research reveals that 83% of single-child parents in India exhibit helicopter parenting behaviors, with Indian adolescents scoring significantly higher (70.73 vs 42.2) on overinvolvement scales compared to American counterparts. Urban areas demonstrate higher prevalence, with 54% of urban parents employing authoritarian parenting styles combined with material indulgence. Six Pocket Syndrome significantly impacts multiple developmental domains-cognitive, emotional, social, and behavioralextending into adulthood with consequences for adult functioning, relationship formation, and societal participation. Helicopter parenting negatively correlates with academic performance despite increased parental investment. Six Pocket Syndrome in India requires multi-level prevention and intervention strategies addressing individual family dynamics, community norms, and policy frameworks. Balanced child welfare policies, parent education programs emphasizing developmental appropriateness and independence training, and educational system modifications promoting holistic development are essential. This research provides a foundation for understanding and addressing one of the most significant contemporary challenges in child development and family functioning in India.

title: Time as a Core Resource: How the Confidant System in Persona 5 Royal Uses Time to Structure Gameplay, Decision Space, and Emotional Experiences
affiliations: and Chalmers University of Technology

detail.title: Time as a Core Resource: How the Confidant System in Persona 5 Royal Uses Time to Structure Gameplay, Decision Space, and Emotional Experiences
detail.abstract: Time in Persona 5 Royal is an explicit, irreversible resource that organizes action and emotion. This paper explains how the Confidant system is designed to utilize this resource to design the loops of gameplay and the decision space, and how this design affects the players in an emotional way. The results demonstrate that the discrete time steps reduce the possibility of choice, impose evident opportunity cost to each action, and make planning integral to play. The in-game time system aligns social progression with the benefits of combat, tying the immediate decision-making with the long-term gains, maintaining momentum, and paradoxes in the narrative are minimized, without taking away the agency of the players. Generally, the explicit and irreversible time budget makes the rules, rewards and feedback coherent and looped, to enhance meaning and emotion, providing a useful principle for creating time-based systems.

title: First-Mover Advantage in Sustainability: An Agent-based Model Perspective

detail.title: First-Mover Advantage in Sustainability: An Agent-based Model Perspective
detail.abstract: This paper utilizes an Agent-Based Model (ABM) to investigate the efficacy of an eco-tax policy in driving corporate green transition within a heterogeneous industry of Green and Brown firms. The model applies a dynamic financial penalty proportional to environmental impact, compelling Brown firms to reallocate capital toward green investment to mitigate their tax burden. Simulation results demonstrate that this mechanism is decisively effective: the eco-tax successfully forces all Brown firms to transition to Green status, achieving complete industry-wide environmental convergence by the simulation’s end. The analysis shows the tax acts as a powerful Pigouvian instrument, accelerating the green transformation and confirming that environmental policy can fundamentally align economic incentives with sustainability objectives. Furthermore, long-term trends reveal that while the tax ensures transition, firms that started Green maintain greater long-term profit stability than those forced to transition, underscoring the enduring competitive advantage of proactive sustainability.

detail.abstract: This contribution assesses the economic and environmental performance of energy-efficiency upgrades in existing buildings, focusing on thermal envelope modernization. Drawing on data from 140 retrofit measures across 57 buildings, it compares lifecycle costs and energy savings under varied component conditions. Results show that exterior wall insulation delivers the highest return on investment, followed by roof insulation and window replacements, while skylight upgrades are least cost-effective. detail.abstract: Most interventions fail to change behavior. We argue that the reason for this failure is that the interventions do not adequately address the type of the underlying problem. We develop a systematic, parsimonious, and generalizable framework that uses a simple survey tool (anamnesis) to identify three types of fundamental problems: awareness, intention, and implementation problems. We then test in an online experiment with 7,500 subjects whether our framework can predict the effectiveness of three typical interventions (reminders, incentives, simplifications) that are designed to address a specific fundamental problem. As hypothesized, we find that the interventions’ effectiveness varies substantially between the different settings, but that our framework can predict this heterogeneity remarkably well: On average, a predicted effectiveness of 10% corresponds to an actual effectiveness of 8.92%. Choosing an intervention based on our framework increases an intervention’s effect size by around 58% compared to randomly choosing one of the tested interventions. We also apply our framework to predict the findings of a large-scale megastudy about booster vaccinations, providing evidence for its external validity for designing effective interventions.

detail.abstract: This paper studies the heterogeneous impact of local government spending across racial groups. An exogenous increase in spending results in significant improvement in White, but not Black or Hispanic, labor market outcomes such as employment rate, weekly hours worked, and labor income. These effects on adults translate into their children's academic performance. White students show significant improvement in test scores, but Black or Hispanic students do not. Consequently, the achievement racial gap widens following an increase in local government spending. These results highlight the possibility that an increase in local government spending could unexpectedly increase intergenerational racial disparity.

title: Nonlinear Estimation of a New Keynesian Model with Endogenous Inflation De-Anchoring
affiliations: Deutsche Bundesbank and University of Kiel

detail.title: Nonlinear Estimation of a New Keynesian Model with Endogenous Inflation De-Anchoring
detail.abstract: We estimate a New Keynesian model that allows endogenous transitions between a target equilibrium, with inflation fluctuating around the central bank’s target and interest rates typically positive, and a low-inflation equilibrium, where the effective lower bound binds and de-anchored expectations keep inflation persistently below target. The model is estimated using Bayesian methods, employing an ensemble MCMC sampler with a particle filter to handle nonlinearities. We find that the United States remained in the target equilibrium after the global financial crisis, the euro area transitioned to the low-inflation equilibrium in 2015, with the subsequent inflation surge initiating a return to the target equilibrium in 2021, and Japan entered the low-inflation equilibrium in the early 2000s. Bayes factors strongly favor the equilibrium-transition model over an alternative specification in which the lower bound binds only occasionally and expectations remain anchored.

detail.title: Peru: Funding and Regulation of Private and Faith-Based Schools
detail.abstract: This report is part of a research project that seeks to understand educational pluralism in Latin America by studying the government funding available for—and legal rules governing the operations of—privately operated elementary and secondary schools. Funding and autonomy are the twin legal levers of educational pluralism. This is because the extent of institutional pluralism in the education context is driven by two factors: First, which types of schools does the law require the government to fund (and at what level)? And, second, to what extent does the law preserve the autonomy of schools (both funded and unfunded) to operate free from government control? In the United States, where private schools are relatively unregulated, debates about private and faith-based education have tended to focus on questions about government funding: How much, if any, should the government fund privately operated schools? In contrast, public funding of private schools has long been a feature of Latin American education policy. Perhaps as a result, education policy debates in Latin America tend to focus on the flip side of the pluralism coin: That is, on the degree of government control of private schools. After briefly describing the elementary and secondary education landscape in one Latin American country, each report then details the legal rules—statutes, regulations, and judicial decisions—that govern the funding and regulation of private and faith-based schools in that context. Read together, these reports shine light on understudied aspects of comparative education policy and highlight potential tradeoffs between the funding and autonomy of non-governmental schools.

affiliations: and University of Dhaka

detail.title: Impact of Domestic Remittances on Financial Inclusion: An Empirical Study of South Asia
detail.abstract: The paper discusses the domestic remittance and financial inclusion nexus, focusing on how domestic remittances in South Asia affect people's use of debit and credit cards, savings accounts, and borrowing options. Remittances are considered a potential driver of financial inclusion for recipients due to their role as a reliable source of income and savings. We investigate this impact using survey data from the World Bank's Global Financial Inclusion (Global Findex) Database for 2014 and 2017. With a set of dummy dependent variables for financial inclusion, we construct probit regression models and regress them on receiving and sending remittances while adjusting for age, gender, education, and income. Results indicate that domestic remittances have a favorable influence on access to debit cards, savings, and borrowing behavior, particularly for remittance senders. However, among remittance recipients, the data indicate a detrimental impact on borrowings and, for some countries, on debit card usage. Furthermore, the results show a very salient impact on credit card behavior for both recipients and senders.

detail.abstract:
The paper proposes a new framework for representing and analyzing the economic process, which promises to integrate different strands developed in the last decades by economic theory and social sciences in general, such as constitutional and institutional economics, transaction costs theories, or behavioral economics, which do not find their proper place in the standard neoclassical model of the economy.

According to this new framework, the economic activity in the traditional sense is only a part of a larger process by which human societies produce and reproduce continuously the conditions of their own survival and expansion. Six categories of factors are identified that are necessary and sufficient to ensure (enlarged) societal reproduction, and all human activities are dedicated to producing and reproducing these six factors of production: nature, labor, fixed capital, the institutional arrangements, knowledge/technology, and the external frontier that controls interactions between one economic and social entity with other similar systems. The production of each factor uses as inputs all other factors, and the whole process of production may be represented as a 6x6 input-output table that depicts the never-ending interchange of flows of factors engendered by the economic and social activity. A production function is to be determined for each factor, having as arguments factors created in a previous cycle or production.

detail.abstract: This study explores the interaction between gamma exposure and investor psychology in the Indian options market, focusing specifically on the NIFTY 50 index options. Gamma, as the second derivative of an option's price with respect to the underlying asset, governs the rate at which Delta changes and plays a critical role in market-maker hedging strategies. This study examines how behavioral biasessuch as overconfidence, herding, loss aversion, and recency biasinteract with Gamma, creating feedback loops that amplify market volatility. By analyzing historical options data, open interest trends, and retail participation metrics from 2018 to 2025, this study demonstrates that integrating behavioral finance insights into quantitative models enhances risk management, pricing accuracy, and strategic decisionmaking in Indian derivative markets.

detail.title: Event-Driven Equity Return Prediction from SEC/Earnings Text with TF-IDF + Logistic Regression, Meta-Labeling, and Cost-Aware Evaluation
detail.abstract: We study whether textual disclosures in SEC and earnings announcements can be transformed into robust, tradable cross-sectional signals. We implement a pipeline: scrape and validate events, align them to prices, generate labels as forward returns, train a TF-IDF + logistic regression baseline with time-based splits, and evaluate with monthly information coefficients (IC), calibration diagnostics, and cost-aware portfolio summaries. We further report multipletesting control via Reality Check / SPA and monitor class-balance drift. Results demonstrate statistically meaningful IC and reasonable gross portfolio characteristics on out-of-sample holdout data, with clear limitations and a path to stronger models (contrastive embeddings, metalabeling and execution refinements).

detail.title: Why EU Revenue Matters: A Case for an EU Digital Levy

publicationDetails.detailsText: European Law Open, volume 3, issue 4, 2024[10.1017/elo.2024.40]

detail.abstract: This Article draws upon and connects three different developments: the 'internationalisation' of tax law and EU tax law, specifically; the increasing digitalisation of the economy, and the European Union's need for more revenue to deal with the financial consequences of the COVID-19 pandemic and other policy priorities. It is explained why the taxation of data per se cannot be addressed at the global level at present and why the focus of research has to lie on the taxation of the different business models of the digital economy. In the absence of a global agreement as to how the digital economy should be taxed, the reaction of the European Union to such a fundamental undertaking remains uncertain and politically contingent on the outcomes of negotiation at the OECD level. Most particularly, on the so-called Pillar One agreement. A seemingly temporal solution to the taxation of the digital economy, the so-called DSTs (Digital Services Taxes) have been adopted by Member States of the EU and third countries, but their future remains uncertain. Amidst these developments, the EU has also looked for ways to increase its resources and to finance its post-Covid ambitious recovery plan. This need has led to a reconsideration of whether EU taxes could finance the EU budget (next to the Union's own resources, which remain for the main part transfers from Member States). In this Article, I argue that beyond tax design considerations and potential constitutional impediments, the EU revenue side should be emphasised in the discussion. Therefore, I suggest that the Union should ensure that at least part of the revenue arising from digital taxation should be channeled to the supranational budget. Whether Pillar One gets adopted or not, the potential introduction of an EU digital levy, ideally by way of an EU tax, could help overcoming several shortcomings of the present tax status quo and could result in an increase of the resources at the disposal of the EU in a fashion compatible with the imperatives of democratic legitimacy.

title: A Lightweight Wild Berry Detector with a Heterogeneous Backbone and Dynamic Feature Interaction
affiliations: Wannan Medical College, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: A Lightweight Wild Berry Detector with a Heterogeneous Backbone and Dynamic Feature Interaction
detail.abstract: Automated detection of wild berries is a pivotal component of precision agriculture. However, its deployment on edge platforms such as unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV) has long been constrained by the trade-off between accuracy and efficiency inherent in existing models. To overcome this bottleneck, this paper proposes a lightweight berry object detection network (LiBerryNet). Through the synergistic design of an innovative backbone, neck, and decoder, it achieves an excellent balance between precision and efficiency at the architectural level. Comprehensive experiments on the publicly available WildBerry dataset demonstrate that LiBerryNet achieves 52.78% mAP50:95 with an exceptionally low computational overhead: merely 0.69M parameters and 1.6G FLOPs. Further visualization and cross-dataset tests confirm robust performance under occlusion, small objects, and extreme lighting conditions, as well as superior generalization. This research provides a high-precision, high-efficiency wild berry detection solution for resource-constrained UAV platforms, with significant application value for advancing smart agriculture and automated harvesting technologies.

title: Lean and Flat Work Together: Lean Startup Method, Organizational Hierarchy, and Startup Success
affiliations: University of Texas at Dallas, Hunan University and Cheung Kong Graduate School of Business

detail.title: Lean and Flat Work Together: Lean Startup Method, Organizational Hierarchy, and Startup Success
detail.abstract: Emphasizing rapid experimentation and data-driven decision-making, the Lean Startup Method (LSM) has become a widely adopted approach to innovation management. While LSM has gained popularity across startups and large enterprises alike, its effectiveness remains inconsistent. This paper argues that the success of LSM depends not only on its technical implementation but also on its alignment with complementary organizational practices. Drawing on a novel panel dataset of about 100,000 U.S.-based startups from 2010 to 2023, we examine whether organizational flatness-measured by the number of distinct hierarchical levels-influences the performance impact of LSM. Using resume-based job role data from Revelio Labs and venture investment data from Pitchbook, we construct firm-year measures of LSM adoption and hierarchy. We find that LSM adoption is significantly more effective in flatter firms, where decentralized decision-making and cross-functional collaboration facilitate rapid experimentation and fast iteration. While flatness alone is not positively associated with firm performance, its combination with LSM predicts higher levels of future funding, faster product iteration, and higher workforce stability. Our findings underscore the importance of organizational complementarity in the successful deployment of digital innovation methods and contribute to the literature on IT-enabled innovation by highlighting how organizational structure conditions the return to agile, data-driven practices.

title: The Rise of the Knowledge Sculptor: A New Archetype for Knowledge Work in the Age of Generative AI
affiliations: Victoria University of Wellington - Te Herenga Waka

detail.title: The Rise of the Knowledge Sculptor: A New Archetype for Knowledge Work in the Age of Generative AI
detail.abstract: In the Generative Age, the nature of knowledge work is transforming. Traditional models that emphasise the organisation and retrieval of pre-existing information are increasingly inadequate in the face of generative AI (GenAI) systems capable of autonomous content creation. This paper introduces the Knowledge Sculptor (KS), a new professional archetype for Human-GenAI collaboration that transforms raw AI output into trustworthy, actionable knowledge. Grounded in a socio-technical perspective, the KS is conceptualised through a framework of competencies, including architecting a vision, iterative dialogue, information sculpting, and curiosity-driven synthesis. A practice-based vignette illustrates the KS role in action, and in a self-referential approach, the paper itself serves as an artefact of the sculpting process it describes.

title: AI Readiness Skills: A Common Minimum Framework for Upskilling Humans
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: AI Readiness Skills: A Common Minimum Framework for Upskilling Humans
detail.abstract:
This paper proposes a framework of a skill-set called "AI Readiness Skills" that every human needs to survive & succeed in the rapidly evolving AI world. The framework addresses four key objectives which are common to all humans: staying safe from AI-related threats, rebuilding careers after AI replaces jobs, retaining current jobs as AI becomes increasingly capable, and qualifying for new jobs in the post-AI economy.
The framework is built as a three-level pyramid with Digital Citizenship & Internet Maturity (DCIM) skills at the bottom, the 4Cs (Critical Thinking, Creativity, Collaboration, and Communication) in the middle, and AI Tools skills at the top. We provide evidence showing why this skill-set is foundational for humans to respond to the ever-increasing threats & opportunities of Artificial Intelligence.

title: Set Shaping Theory: An Extension of Classical Information Theory
affiliations: Unaffiliated Author and

detail.title: Set Shaping Theory: An Extension of Classical Information Theory
detail.abstract: The Set Shaping Theory (SST) introduces a combinatorial framework that reformulates the foundations of lossless data compression. While Shannon's classical theory defines coding efficiency in probabilistic terms, SST operates on the structural properties of the sequence space itself. By reshaping the domain of sequences through invertible transformations, SST achieves a reduction in average empirical entropy without requiring prior knowledge of source statistics. This paper outlines the conceptual transition from probabilistic to combinatorial measures of information and discusses how this approach complements, rather than violates, the Shannon framework.
